import sys, json, uuid, datetime, hashlib

# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so
# each one is per-INSTANCE configuration -- two collectors in one colony are
# tuned apart, and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a colony-wide
# environment. The literal beside each name is the shipped default; it is the
# same number the template config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test
# pins the three against each other.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _float(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return float(v)


def _str(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    return "" if v is None else str(v)


def _list(key, default):
    """A declared name list. The ruling writes it as a JSON array
    (`["web_search", "web_fetch"]`); a comma string is read the same way, because
    `override_params` reaches this knob as a config line somebody types and
    `recoverability` one screen down already reads that way. Anything else is
    EMPTY rather than half-read -- a declaration that lost half its names would
    hand a model a smaller tool set with nobody saying so.
    """
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        v = v.split(",")
    if not isinstance(v, list):
        return []
    return [str(n).strip() for n in v if str(n).strip()]

MEMORY_TIER = _str("memory_tier", "")

# agent can ever DECIDE to ask memory about a time RANGE -- the half of the

# emits a `memory_recall` tool_call, the dispatcher routes it by name like any

# owns the recall port (R-OS-5), so it serves the call itself and hands the
# answer back into its own fan-in -- the round ends where it began (R-OS-2).

MEMORY_CALL_TIER = _str("memory_call_tier", "1")

# at the seam, so the seam is what ends it: at the cap the assembled context
# leaves on the answer lane instead of asking again. No dispatcher and no edge
# condition is needed to stop a runaway loop.
MAX_ITER = _int("max_iter", 8)
# --- round robustness (GH #103) ----------------------------------------------
# A round whose fan-in can never complete (a result lost in flight) must not
# park forever. When its last progress -- the newest recorded_at of its rows --
# is older than this window AND the fan-in is incomplete, the NEXT message that
# reaches this cell anyway (the next result, the next turn, a sweep) closes it:
# the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results and the round fires
# through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. Pure arithmetic, no timer
# of the template's own, no model judgement.
ROUND_IDLE_MS = _int("round_idle_ms", 120000)

# only what a close batch already carried out of this hive (the `batched`
# ledger row written beside the write emission) AND whose delivery is older
# than this gate. Without a ledger row nothing is ever pruned -- rather grow
# than silently lose a turn. Store rows are cell state inside the cell.db,
# not {root} files; the substrate's No-Delete-Policy is about files.
PRUNE_AFTER_MS = _int("prune_after_ms", 604800000)

# The ONLY path from a conversation into the episodes table. Every STORED turn
# -- the inbound one and the answer -- leaves again on its own route as ONE
# message per turn, so an episode of a turn exists AT the turn instead of at
# the night close: the difference between a question about the last exchange
# being answerable and being answered wrongly.
#
# LLM-free, and no longer a second way of saying what the close lane says: the
# close lane hands out a day for whoever archives one, this lane hands out
# turns for whoever keeps episodes, and the two documents are different on
# purpose.
#
# It ships ON. Since Q11 nothing else writes episodes, so a shipped default of
# "off" is a shipped agent that remembers nothing; switching it off means the
# conversation reaches no memory at all, not that it reaches one later. Both
# spellings of off work, "" and "0", because an operator who blanks a line and
# an operator who writes a zero mean the same thing.
#

# is handed out while `episode_written` reads 0, and the guarded update that
# sets it rides in the SAME emission as the episode it covers.
TURN_WRITE = _str("turn_write", "1")
# --- the inline extraction contract (GH #525) --------------------------------
# WHETHER this collector asks its brain for the annotation the memory hive's
# `in_remember` lane reads. It is a template promise and not a person's charter,
# so it is delivered by the cell that assembles the prompt rather than pasted
# into an identity by hand -- and it is written on EVERY assembly rather than

# COMPOSITE decides: `talky` cuts the block and switches this on, `cogny` has no

INLINE_EXTRACTION = _str("inline_extraction", "")

CONTEXT_WINDOW = _int("context_window", 0)

CURATE_SOFT = _float("curate_soft", 0.50)

RECOVERABILITY = _str("recoverability", "")
# The thread tool: what a stub is worth is what it can bring back. Empty

THREAD_RECALL = _str("thread_recall", "1")

THREAD_RECALL_BUDGET = _float("thread_recall_budget", 0.20)

TOOL_MENU = _str("tool_menu", "")
# What survives of a stubbed declaration beside its name. A stub the model

def boundary_of(ref):
    """The close arrival time riding in a close chain's hop id
    ('close-<session>|<B>'). A ref without one is the pre-#76 shape -- at most
    one in-flight close across an upgrade -- and falls back to now."""
    parts = ref.rsplit("|", 1)
    return parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 and parts[1] else now

def park():
    """Terminal by design: an incomplete fan-in and a lost guard race emit
    NOTHING, exactly like the store-backed tool loop this grew out of."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def head(route, ph="", tid=None, extra=None):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the port edges read. A missing
    hop key makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge --
    so keys are always present and empty rather than absent."""
    out = {"route": route, "phase": ph, "turn_id": turn_id if tid is None else tid,
           "session_id": session, "iter": str(it)}
    if extra:
        out.update(extra)
    return out


def store_op(args, ph, tid=None, extra=None):
    return {"header": head("cstore", ph, tid, extra),
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "c-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def cstore_bundle(calls, ph, tid=None, extra=None):
    """GH #419 -- N ops in ONE message, answered in ONE reply (#295).

    `calls` is [(tool_call_id, args), ...] in the order the ops should run. The
    store runs them sequentially over its one connection, so a select at the end
    sees the inserts in front of it -- which is the whole reason the round table
    needs no guarded update to elect a firing hop any more.

    A bundle is TWO OR MORE tool_calls (`tool_call_turn_count`, store cell.rs):
    a single call would come back as an ordinary single-op reply, so the caller
    of this helper always writes at least two.
    """
    return {"header": head("cstore", ph, tid, extra),
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in calls]}


def results_by_id(doc):
    """One entry per leg of a bundle reply, keyed by `tool_call_id` (#295): the
    turns carry the payloads, the top-level `results[]` slot carries each op's
    own `operation`/`rows_affected`/`error_code`, and this reads both so nothing
    downstream has to know there were two arrays."""
    out = {}
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "operation": "", "error_code": ""}
    for r in doc.get("results") or []:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                             {"payload": None, "operation": "", "error_code": ""})
        leg["operation"] = str(r.get("operation") or "")
        leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
    return out


def bundle_rows_of(doc, cid):
    """The row list one leg of a bundle came back with -- [] for anything else,
    the same reading `rows_of` gives a single-op reply."""
    p = (results_by_id(doc).get(cid) or {}).get("payload")
    return p if isinstance(p, list) else []


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def round_sets(rows, iter_):
    """The fan-in state of ONE iteration, read from the slate: the call ids the
    assistant expects, the ids that answered, and the newest write time of the
    round's rows -- its last PROGRESS. A row that cannot be dated still counts
    as progress-less rather than as old: an undatable round is never closed
    (the R-P3 direction -- what the policy cannot date, the policy leaves in
    its pre-#103 behaviour)."""
    expected, received, progress = set(), set(), ""
    for r in rows:
        if int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) != iter_:
            continue
        role = r.get("role")
        if role not in ("assistant", "tool"):
            continue
        rec = str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
        if rec > progress:
            progress = rec
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if role == "assistant":
            items = t if isinstance(t, list) else [t]
            expected.update(x.get("id", "") for x in items
                            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_call"
                            and x.get("id"))
        else:
            # A result may bring MORE than one turn (GH #252), and every id in
            # it answers a call: a fan-in that reads only the first waits for a
            # result that has already arrived.
            items = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])
            received.update(x.get("id") for x in items
                            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("id"))
    return expected, received, progress


def re_check(r):
    """The scoped re-check of one open round (GH #103): the REGULAR
    round-check, run under the round's own turn, iteration and session -- the
    internal edge promotes all three from the hop. The check itself decides on
    full progress; this only names the round worth asking about."""
    tid = str(r.get("turn_id") or "")
    extra = {"iter": str(int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0))}
    s = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
    if s:
        extra["session_id"] = s
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                     "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired",
                                 "recorded_at"],
                     "where": {"turn_id": tid}}, "round-check", tid, extra=extra)


def lost_results(missing):
    """Synthetic error tool_results for calls whose results never arrived
    (GH #103) -- the dispatcher-lid pattern: the tool_call_id is kept, so the
    round becomes fan-in-complete and fires through the REGULAR guard instead
    of through second machinery. The row-level `lost` marker lets the seam say
    hop.round_stale=1; it is store bookkeeping and is stripped from the wire."""
    return [round_park("tool",
                         {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": mid,
                          "text": "tool result lost: the round went idle before"
                                  " this call's result arrived",
                          "lost": 1},
                         "round-check") for mid in sorted(missing)]


def round_park(role, turn, ph, iter_=None, tid=None, rec=None, head_tid=None,
               fired=0):
    """GH #419 -- park a round row AND read the slate back, in ONE message.

    Same row as `round_insert` writes, same columns as `round_select` reads,
    and the two used to be two messages plus a guarded update between them. The
    store runs a bundle's ops in order over its one connection, so the trailing
    select sees the insert in front of it: of N legs parking concurrently
    exactly ONE reads a complete set, and that one fires. No guard row to win,
    no message to win it with.
    """
    rid = turn_id if tid is None else tid
    return cstore_bundle(
        [("c-" + ph + "-row",
          {"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
           "row": {"turn_id": rid, "session_id": session,
                   "iter": it if iter_ is None else iter_,
                   "role": role, "turn": json.dumps(turn), "fired": fired,
                   "recorded_at": now if rec is None else rec}}),
         ("c-" + ph + "-read",
          {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
           "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired", "recorded_at"],
           "where": {"turn_id": rid}})],
        ph, rid if head_tid is None else head_tid)


def text_of(doc, origin):
    """The last turn of that origin -- a chat surface delivers one, a batch
    ingress may deliver several and the newest is the one being answered."""
    found = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("origin") == origin and m.get("type") in ("text", None):
            found = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    return found


def any_text(doc):
    """The last turn that carries text at all, whatever its origin and type
    say. Two arrivals need this: an EVENT from another agent carries the role
    of ITS conversation, not of this one -- and an ERRAND addressed by tool
    name arrives as a `tool_call` turn whose text is the raw arguments. Both
    times the text IS the message, and a turn written with empty content would
    be a question nobody asked."""
    found = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        text = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
        if text:
            found = text
    return found


def window_of(rows):
    """The rolling short-term window. Two cuts, both deterministic:

    the TURN cap already ran in the store (order by id desc, limit N), the BYTE
    cap runs here from the newest turn backwards. Whatever the byte cap cannot
    afford is dropped as a WHOLE turn and everything older with it -- a window
    with a hole in the middle is not a conversation. The newest turn is kept
    unconditionally: the turn being answered is never the one evicted.

    Nothing is deleted. Eviction is a READ-TIME cut over an append-only table;
    the durable record of a conversation belongs to the memory hive, not here.

    `deferred` counts the mid-round turns riding along for the first time
    (GH #103) -- the seam reports them as round_deferred=1 and clears the
    stamp in the same multi-send.
    """
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("id", "")))
    capped = 1 if len(rows) >= WINDOW_TURNS else 0
    kept, spent, dropped, deferred = [], 0, 0, 0
    for r in reversed(rows):
        content = str(r.get("content") or "")[:TURN_CHARS]
        cost = len(content)
        if kept and spent + cost > WINDOW_BYTES:
            dropped = len(rows) - len(kept)
            break
        # The default STAYS here (GH #282), unlike the one the close lane had:
        # `leg-window` is read by `brain_message` and by nothing else -- no
        # write path ever sees it. A turn shown to the model has to be
        # attributed to one of the two voices of a chat completion, and a row
        # that is not the agent's own is the other side of the conversation.
        # Nothing downstream turns this default into an episode.
        kept.append({"role": str(r.get("role") or "user"), "text": content,
                     "consult_id": str(r.get("consult_id") or "")})
        if int(r.get("deferred", 0) or 0) == 1:
            deferred += 1
        spent += cost
    kept.reverse()
    return {"turns": kept, "bytes": spent, "dropped": dropped, "capped": capped,
            "deferred": deferred}


def leg_of(rows, role):
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("role") == role:
            try:
                return json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
            except Exception:
                return None
    return None


def cost_of(turn):
    return len(str(turn.get("text", "") or "")) if isinstance(turn, dict) else 0


def thread_of(rows):
    """The tool round in PLAIN order: per iteration the assistant turn that
    asked, then the tool results that answered -- and BOUNDED, because a single
    tool result can be larger than the whole window it is entering (GH #91).

    Two cuts, the same discipline as the conversation window: a per-item
    character cap on tool RESULT texts, then a byte cap over the whole round
    counted from the newest iteration backwards. What the byte cap cannot
    afford falls as a whole ITERATION -- a tool_result whose tool_call was
    dropped is not a round, it is a malformed turn for every provider. Nothing
    is deleted: the full text stays readable in the `round` table.

    A synthetic stand-in (GH #103) travels only while no real result for the
    same call exists: the store keeps both rows, the wire carries one result
    per call id, and the `lost` marker never leaves the store. A stand-in that
    travels in the iteration being fired makes the emission stale.

    Every item is tagged with the iteration it belongs to (`_it`), so the
    curator can spare the newest rounds; the tag is bookkeeping and is stripped
    with the other private markers before anything leaves.

    Returns (items, dropped, capped, stale, names, recalled, tp). The last three
    exist for the curator and for nobody else: the tool NAME behind every call
    id -- the only place a recoverability class can be decided from -- the call
    ids a `thread_recall` already brought back in this turn, and the newest
    provider token count this turn has seen.
    """
    items = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") in ("assistant", "tool")]
    items.sort(key=lambda r: (int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0),
                              0 if r.get("role") == "assistant" else 1))
    groups, capped = [], 0
    names, recalled, tp = {}, set(), 0
    for r in items:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        turns = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])
        cut = []
        for x in turns:
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_call":
                # The tool NAME lives in the provider's `function` object, and
                # that object IS the text of a tool_call turn. Reading it here
                # is the whole of B1: the class of a result is DECLARED per tool
                # and looked up by name, never inferred from the payload.
                if x.get("tp"):
                    try:
                        tp = max(tp, int(x.get("tp") or 0))
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                try:
                    fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
                except Exception:
                    fn = {}
                if isinstance(fn, dict):
                    cid, nm = str(x.get("id") or ""), str(fn.get("name", "") or "")
                    if cid and nm:
                        names[cid] = nm
                    if nm == TR_NAME:
                        try:
                            a = json.loads(fn.get("arguments") or "{}")
                        except Exception:
                            a = {}
                        if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("call_id"):
                            recalled.add(str(a.get("call_id")))
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "text":
                # An interim answer (R-CG-3) left on the answer lane and the
                # in_answer lane already wrote it into the WINDOW. Repeating it
                # here would show it twice -- and it would stand between an
                # assistant turn and the tool results that answer it, which
                # every provider rejects.
                continue
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_result":
                text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
                if len(text) > TOOL_CHARS:
                    x = dict(x, text=text[:TOOL_CHARS])
                    capped = 1
            if isinstance(x, dict):
                x = dict(x, _it=int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0))
            cut.append(x)
        iter_ = int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0)
        if groups and groups[-1][0] == iter_:
            groups[-1][1].extend(cut)
        else:
            groups.append([iter_, list(cut)])
    stale, total = 0, 0
    for iter_, group in groups:
        real = {x.get("id") for x in group
                if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_result"
                and not x.get("lost")}
        cut, seen = [], set()
        for x in group:
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("lost"):
                if x.get("id") in real or x.get("id") in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(x.get("id"))
                if iter_ == it:
                    stale = 1
                x = {k: v for k, v in x.items() if k != "lost"}
            cut.append(x)
        group[:] = cut
        total += len(cut)
    kept, spent = [], 0
    for _, group in reversed(groups):
        cost = sum(cost_of(x) for x in group)
        if kept and spent + cost > ROUND_BYTES:
            capped = 1
            break
        kept[0:0] = group
        spent += cost
    return kept, total - len(kept), capped, stale, names, recalled, tp


def toks(chars):
    """Characters to tokens, as a deliberate LOWER bound. Anthropic changed the
    tokenizer with Claude 4.7+ and the SAME text now yields ~30 % more tokens,
    so `chars/4` is systematically low -- which is the only direction an
    estimate may err in here: a low estimate curates too LATE, never too early,
    and never on a window that did not need it."""
    return chars // 4


def rec_of(x, names):
    """The recoverability class of one tool result. Declared per tool name;
    everything not named is `unique` and is therefore never elided. That default
    is the whole safety property: an undeclared tool costs context, never
    correctness."""
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    if names.get(cid) == TR_NAME:
        # A recall is what a stub points AT. Eliding it is the thrashing loop
        # Claude Code and Gemini CLI both had to retrofit a latch against.
        return "unique"
    return REC_MAP.get(names.get(cid, ""), "unique")


def stub_of(x, cls, names):
    """Restorable compression, Manus' shape: the payload leaves, its key stays.
    The name is a content HASH, so the same payload elided twice reads as the
    same reference (free dedup inside one window), and the line says in plain
    words how to get the original back -- a stub without a way back is just a
    loss with better manners."""
    text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    return dict(x, text=("[elided tool_result %s - %d chars - tool=%s - kind=%s"
                         " - sha256:%s - recall: thread_recall(call_id=\"%s\")]"
                         % (cid, len(text), names.get(cid, "?"), cls, digest, cid)))


def args_stub_of(x):
    """Stage 3: the ARGUMENTS of an old call leave, the call itself stays. That
    asymmetry is the point (Anthropic's `clear_tool_inputs: false`): the record
    of WHAT was done is what stops an agent from doing it a second time, and it
    costs almost nothing to keep."""
    try:
        fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return x
    if not isinstance(fn, dict):
        return x
    raw = str(fn.get("arguments", "") or "")
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    fn = dict(fn, arguments=("[elided arguments - %d chars - recall:"
                             " thread_recall(call_id=\"%s\")]" % (len(raw), cid)))
    return dict(x, text=json.dumps(fn))


def clean(items):
    """Every private marker off, in one place. `lost`, `tr`, `tp` and `_it` are
    this cell's bookkeeping; a provider never sees a word of it."""
    return [({k: v for k, v in x.items() if k not in PRIVATE}
             if isinstance(x, dict) else x) for x in items]


def fn_of(t):
    """The function object of one provider-native declaration.

    Two shapes travel in the wild and both are legal input: the full envelope
    `{"type": "function", "function": {...}}` the reference templates seed, and
    the bare `{"name": ..., "parameters": ...}` some providers take. Reading
    both here is what keeps the tool stage from silently skipping a whole menu
    because it was written in the other spelling."""
    if isinstance(t, dict) and isinstance(t.get("function"), dict):
        return t["function"]
    return t if isinstance(t, dict) else {}


def tool_name_of(t):
    return str(fn_of(t).get("name", "") or "")


def tool_stub_of(t):
    """Stage 4: the SCHEMA of a declaration leaves, its name and one line of
    description stay -- the same asymmetry stage 3 draws over a tool_call, and
    for the same reason. A model that can still read what a tool is FOR can ask
    for the schema back; a model whose tool vanished cannot ask for anything.

    `parameters` becomes the empty object schema rather than disappearing: a
    declaration without it is not a declaration any provider accepts, and a
    curation that produced a rejected request would have traded a large prompt
    for no answer at all."""
    fn = fn_of(t)
    name = tool_name_of(t)
    desc = " ".join(str(fn.get("description", "") or "").split())
    if len(desc) > TOOL_DESC_CHARS:
        desc = desc[:TOOL_DESC_CHARS].rstrip() + "..."
    hint = ("[schema elided - recall: thread_recall(call_id=\"tool:%s\")]" % name)
    stub = dict(fn, description=((desc + " " if desc else "") + hint),
                parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}})
    if isinstance(t, dict) and isinstance(t.get("function"), dict):
        return dict(t, function=stub)
    return stub


def tools_slot(tools):
    """The menu as the `system.tools` subtree the `llm` cell reads: one leaf per
    tool, keyed by its name, each holding the provider-native object as a JSON
    string. `$replace` makes the subtree exactly this -- a menu that is upserted
    leaf by leaf would keep every declaration the collector decided to drop,
    durably, which is the opposite of curation."""
    slot = {"$replace": True}
    for t in tools:
        name = tool_name_of(t)
        if name:
            slot[name] = {"text": json.dumps(t)}
    return slot


def provider_tool_of(schema):
    """One `{name, description, parameters}` declaration in the envelope a
    provider wants (GH #464).

    The tools hive answers provider-NEUTRAL on purpose: a hive that wrapped
    would be a hive that has to be told which provider its caller talks to,
    which is a second thing every caller would have to tell it and a first thing
    it would be wrong about. So the wrapping happens here, on the side that
    knows its provider -- and it produces exactly the shape `fn_of` above reads,
    which is what lets an asked-for menu and a typed one meet the same curator.
    """
    params = schema.get("parameters")
    return {"type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": str(schema.get("name") or ""),
                "description": str(schema.get("description") or ""),
                "parameters": (params if isinstance(params, dict)
                               else {"type": "object", "properties": {}})}}


def self_tool_menu():
    """The tools this collector answers ITSELF, provider-native (GH #512).

    Two of the names on the menu are not the parent's. `memory_recall` is served
    out of this cell's own recall port and `thread_recall` out of its own slate;
    the composite around it routes both here BY NAME, and no tools hive has -- or
    could have -- a declaration for either. `templates/talky/template.json`
    already states the rule: a tool the composite IMPLEMENTS is topology, and its
    schema ships with the composite. What it did not state is WHERE, and the
    answer it shipped with was wrong in a way nothing measured: the two
    declarations were SEED rows in the brain's own `cell.db`.

    A seed is written once, at birth. `tools_slot` is a `$replace`, so the first
    menu tick replaced the whole subtree with what the tools hive had answered --
    and the two names nobody can answer for went with it. A grown agent lost its
    memory tool minutes into its life, kept the whole recall chain below it wired
    and idle, and said its memory was not reachable, which was true and unasked.

    WHICH of the two a collector declares is not a new switch. It is the two
    switches that already decide whether the lane is answered at all instead of
    refused with a typed error: `memory_call_tier` (empty switches the tool off)
    and `thread_recall`. A collector that declares a tool it would refuse and one
    that refuses a tool it declared are the same defect from two sides.

    INTERIM, and pinned while it lasts (GH #552). The `memory_recall` schema
    below is a HAND-TYPED projection of ANOTHER template's contract:
    `memory-hive` names seven context keys on `in_query`, and only three of them
    are the model's -- `query`, `window_from` and `window_to`, which leave here
    as `hop.recall_query`, `hop.recall_window_from` and `hop.recall_window_to`
    and are promoted into context by the port edge. The other four are filled
    BESIDE the model and must not become arguments: `memory_tier` is this cell's
    own `memory_call_tier` knob (a model could otherwise ask for a depth the
    instance was tuned away from), `recall_as_of` is the edge's empty string,
    which the hive reads as "now", and `audience_now` and `channel` come off the
    asking round -- who is present is the gate on every read, and a question
    without it is refused (`missing_audience`, `missing_channel`) rather than
    answered unfiltered. Nothing but
    `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh552_the_recall_schema_is_pinned_to_the_contract.rs`
    holds the two artefacts together, and it goes red the moment either side
    moves. Both it and this entry go when #552 lands and the hive declares
    `memory_recall` itself, on an `in_schemas` of its own.

    One thing that pin RECORDS rather than repairs: the two window bounds are
    declared here as independently optional, while `read_window` in the recall
    cell refuses a HALF-OPEN window (`half_open_window`, pinned by
    `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/p15_recall_window.rs`) -- a model that names one
    bound buys a refusal it cannot see coming. Saying so is a change to what the
    model reads, and on a released template that is a version digit plus a ref
    cascade for one sentence that #552 will write ONCE, in the hive that
    enforces it. So it is written down where it is true and carried, not fixed
    in the copy.
    """
    out = []
    if MEMORY_CALL_TIER:
        out.append(provider_tool_of({
            "name": "memory_recall",
            "description": "Ask long-term memory about something, optionally"
                           " restricted to a time range.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "query": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "what to look for"},
                    "window_from": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "ISO-8601 start of the time range"
                                       " (optional)"},
                    "window_to": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "ISO-8601 end of the time range"
                                       " (optional)"}},
                "required": ["query"]}}))
    if THREAD_RECALL:
        out.append(provider_tool_of({
            "name": TR_NAME,
            "description": "Bring back the full text of a tool result that was"
                           " elided from this turn's context.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "call_id": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "the id printed in the [elided ...]"
                                       " stub"},
                    "round": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "an iteration number, to get a whole"
                                       " round back"},
                    "query": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "a substring to look for in this turn's"
                                       " results"}}}}))
    return out


def tool_schema_text(name):
    """The way back for a stubbed declaration, out of the menu this cell already
    holds: no store read, no round row, no budget wall -- a schema is small and
    a model that is asking for one is about to use it."""
    for t in TOOLS:
        if tool_name_of(t) == name:
            return json.dumps(t)
    return ("thread recall found no tool declaration named '%s' in this"
            " collector's menu" % name)


def sys_stub_of(path, text):
    """Stage 5: an over-size `system.*` leaf of this cell's OWN making is cut to
    its head and says so.

    It is cut rather than replaced by a reference, and that is the safety
    property: `system.*` is upserted per slot path in the brain, so a leaf this
    cell writes OVERWRITES the durable one -- a stub with no text would revoke
    somebody's state instead of shortening one prompt. Only slots this cell
    re-derives from live state every round are candidates (`SYS_KEEP` holds
    every family it does not own), so the cut lasts exactly one round and the
    next assembly writes whatever is true then."""
    head_ = text[:CURATE_SLOT_CHARS].rstrip()
    return ("%s\n[system slot '%s' cut: %d of %d characters shown, re-derived"
            " in full next round]" % (head_, path, len(head_), len(text)))


def curate(msgs, names, recalled, sysm, tools, tp):
    """The curator (B3): the window as a BUDGET PROJECTION, rebuilt at every
    assembly rather than folded at a threshold.

    Three properties make it different from every compaction in the field:

    1. **It runs always, not at a cliff.** A procedure that only starts at
       50-90 % fill has to compress very much into very little in ONE step, in
       the hot path, with one attempt and no way back. This one moves small
       pieces every round.
    2. **It costs no model call.** Nothing is paraphrased, so nothing can be
       paraphrased WRONG: the failure class "the fold dropped exactly the detail
       I needed later" cannot occur, because no text is ever rewritten. What
       leaves is a payload whose class says it is recoverable; what stays is
       every word the model may still need to be right.
    3. **Everything it removes leaves a key.** `thread_recall` is the way back,
       and the difference between "condensed" and "lost".

    Stages, cheapest and safest first. After each one the projection is measured
    again and the work stops as soon as it fits -- the curator does the least
    that is enough.

    | stage | what leaves | what stays |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | `tool_result` payloads whose class is `env` | the stub, the call, the name |
    | 2 | `tool_result` payloads whose class is `repeatable` | the stub, the call, the name |
    | 3 | `tool_call` ARGUMENTS of old calls | the call and its name |
    | 4 | the SCHEMA of a declaration unused for KEEP_ROUNDS | the name and one line |
    | 5 | the tail of an over-size `system.*` slot of this cell's own | the head |

    Stages 4 and 5 are GH #451, and they are what makes the arithmetic honest:
    `tools[]` counts towards the projection now. It never did, and it is the
    largest block in a real prompt -- so a curator could sit at `hard`, out of
    stages, having elided everything it was allowed to touch, while the single
    biggest consumer of the window sat outside its sums.

    Never touched, at any stage or budget: the conversation window (user and
    assistant turns), the `SYS_KEEP` families of `system.*` -- instructions,
    identity, persona, handover -- the tool_call NAMES, the newest KEEP_ROUNDS
    iterations verbatim, every result whose class is `unique`, and every tool
    USED inside those iterations. That list is the prologue protection of the
    CWL paper, and it is also the reason the invariance gate holds: constraints,
    numbers and time markers live in exactly those places, and the curator has
    no path to them.

    MESSAGE VALIDITY BEATS MESSAGE COUNT, and it is a rule rather than a
    consequence: no stage removes a ROW. Stages 1 and 2 replace a payload and
    leave the `tool_result` standing under its own call id, stage 3 empties an
    argument string, and stages 4 and 5 never touch `messages[]` at all -- so
    every `tool_result` in the projection keeps the assistant `tool_call` that
    asked for it. A projection one row smaller and structurally invalid is
    refused by every provider, which makes it infinitely more expensive than the
    window it was shrinking.

    Returns (msgs, sysm, tools, report).
    """
    report = {"tokens_window": "0", "tokens_projected": "0",
              "tokens_estimated": "1" if not tp else "0",
              "curate_mark": "none", "curate_stage": "0",
              "curate_elided": "0", "curate_saved": "0",
              "curate_tools": "0", "curate_slots": "0"}

    def finish(sysm):
        """The budget sentence, at EVERY exit and not only at the busy one.

        It is a `system.*` slot, and `system.*` is upserted per slot path in the
        brain -- so a slot written only while the window is full would stand
        there for the rest of the cell's life quoting the number of the last
        turn that happened to be busy. Durable state is revoked, never merely
        abandoned (GH #259): with the sentence switched off the leaf travels
        EMPTY, and an empty leaf contributes nothing to the prompt.

        With curation itself off (`context_window` 0) no leaf travels at all --
        that cell is byte-for-byte the one that shipped before GH #451, and a
        slot it never wrote needs no revoking.
        """
        if CONTEXT_WINDOW <= 0:
            return sysm
        used = int(report["tokens_projected"])
        line = ("" if CURATE_BUDGET_LINE in ("", "0") else
                "Context budget: %d of %d tokens used, %d left."
                % (used, CONTEXT_WINDOW, max(CONTEXT_WINDOW - used, 0)))
        out = dict(sysm or {})
        out["budget"] = {"text": line}
        return out

    def sys_chars():
        """`system.*` AND the declarations. The tool block was outside this sum
        until #451, which is how a window could be 60 % declarations and read as
        comfortable."""
        return (len(json.dumps(sysm)) if sysm else 0) + sum(
            len(json.dumps(t)) for t in tools)

    def size():
        return toks(sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs) + sys_chars())

    before_chars = sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs) + sys_chars()
    window = tp if tp else size()
    report["tokens_window"] = str(window)
    report["tokens_projected"] = str(size())
    if CONTEXT_WINDOW <= 0:
        # Off. The knob is empty, so nothing about this cell moves -- the caps
        # above stay the only bound, exactly as before wave 11.
        return clean(msgs), finish(sysm), tools, report
    soft = CONTEXT_WINDOW * CURATE_SOFT
    hard = CONTEXT_WINDOW * CURATE_HARD
    report["curate_mark"] = ("hard" if window >= hard else
                             ("soft" if window >= soft else "none"))
    if window < soft:
        return clean(msgs), finish(sysm), tools, report
    # The newest KEEP_ROUNDS iterations are verbatim whatever the budget says
    # (CompactionRL keeps k=2). An iteration without a tag is a conversation
    # turn and was never a candidate.
    floor = it - KEEP_ROUNDS + 1
    elided = 0
    stubbed_tools, stubbed_slots = 0, 0

    def old(x):
        return isinstance(x, dict) and "_it" in x and int(x.get("_it", 0)) < floor

    def fresh_names():
        """Which tools this window has ACTUALLY used inside the kept rounds.

        The rule is usage and nothing else -- no ranking, no model, no
        similarity. A call id carries its tool name (`names`), and an item
        carries the iteration it belongs to, so "used recently" is a lookup over
        two facts the cell already holds. A tool used inside `KEEP_ROUNDS` is
        one the model is working with right now, and taking its schema away
        mid-task is how an agent forgets how to do the thing it is doing."""
        used = set()
        for x in msgs:
            if not isinstance(x, dict) or old(x):
                continue
            nm = names.get(str(x.get("id") or ""))
            if nm:
                used.add(nm)
        # The tool a stub points AT is never a candidate: eliding the way back
        # is the thrashing loop, one level up from stage 1's version of it.
        used.add(TR_NAME)
        return used

    for stage in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5):
        if size() < soft:
            break
        report["curate_stage"] = str(stage)
        out = []
        for x in msgs:
            if not old(x):
                out.append(x)
                continue
            if stage in (1, 2) and x.get("type") == "tool_result":
                cls = rec_of(x, names)
                # A call already brought back by `thread_recall` is elided
                # whatever its class says: its payload stands in the window
                # once already, and "one representation per prompt" is what
                # keeps a recall from doubling what it recovered. The stub
                # stays as the ANSWER to its call -- dropping the row outright
                # would leave a tool_call unanswered, which every provider
                # rejects.
                forced = str(x.get("id") or "") in recalled
                want = "env" if stage == 1 else "repeatable"
                if (cls == want or forced) and not str(x.get("text", "")).startswith("[elided"):
                    out.append(stub_of(x, "recalled" if forced else cls, names))
                    elided += 1
                    continue
            if stage in (4, 5):
                out.append(x)
                continue
            if stage == 3 and x.get("type") == "tool_call":
                try:
                    fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
                except Exception:
                    fn = {}
                raw = str(fn.get("arguments", "") or "") if isinstance(fn, dict) else ""
                # Only when the arguments are bigger than the stub that would
                # replace them: a cut that costs bytes is not a cut.
                if len(raw) > 200:
                    out.append(args_stub_of(x))
                    elided += 1
                    continue
            out.append(x)
        msgs = out
        if stage == 4 and tools:
            # THE LARGEST BLOCK IN THE PROMPT (GH #451). Deterministic: a
            # declaration whose tool was not called inside the newest
            # KEEP_ROUNDS iterations is stubbed to its name and one line, and
            # `thread_recall(call_id="tool:<name>")` hands the schema back out
            # of the menu this cell holds -- no store read, no round row.
            keep = fresh_names()
            cut = []
            for t in tools:
                nm = tool_name_of(t)
                if nm and nm not in keep and "[schema elided" not in json.dumps(t):
                    cut.append(tool_stub_of(t))
                    stubbed_tools += 1
                    continue
                cut.append(t)
            tools = cut
        if stage == 5 and CURATE_SLOT_CHARS > 0 and sysm:
            # `system.*`, and only the slots this cell WRITES: every other
            # family is in SYS_KEEP, because a leaf sent here overwrites the
            # durable one in the brain and a curator must never revoke somebody
            # else's state to shorten one prompt.
            cut = dict(sysm)
            for slot in sorted(cut):
                if slot in SYS_KEEP or not isinstance(cut[slot], dict):
                    continue
                node = dict(cut[slot])
                text = str(node.get("text", "") or "")
                if len(text) > CURATE_SLOT_CHARS:
                    node["text"] = sys_stub_of(slot, text)
                    cut[slot] = node
                    stubbed_slots += 1
            sysm = cut
    report["curate_elided"] = str(elided)
    report["curate_tools"] = str(stubbed_tools)
    report["curate_slots"] = str(stubbed_slots)
    report["curate_saved"] = str(
        before_chars - sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs) - sys_chars())
    report["tokens_projected"] = str(size())
    # SAY the budget, do not only enforce it ("The Sleeping Agent" measured
    # 3.05 % -> 62.39 % from a prompt fix alone: a generator told where it
    # stands behaves differently from one that is silently cut). One
    # deterministic sentence out of numbers the report already holds -- no
    # model, nothing to drift. Its own ~70 characters are not inside the count
    # it quotes, which is the direction every estimate in this cell errs in.
    return clean(msgs), finish(sysm), tools, report


def cap_text(val):
    """A rendered block enters the window bounded (GH #91), never rewritten.
    The full bundle stays where the memory hive put it."""
    return (val, 0) if len(val) <= MEMORY_CHARS else (val[:MEMORY_CHARS], 1)


def system_of(mem):
    """What is LEFT of the memory slot once the bundle became evidence: the
    revocation, and nothing else (GH #278).

    THE DATA HALF MOVED INTO THE ROUND. Until this wave the recall bundle was
    written into `system.memory` and stayed there -- durable state of the agent,
    upserted per slot path, sitting where its instructions live. It is not that:
    it is the answer to one question asked once, and it now travels where an
    answer belongs, as the `memory_recall` tool result of THIS turn (see
    `brain_message`). Three defects close with the move -- a model can see where
    the bundle came from, its bytes are attributable in the projection instead
    of an anonymous lump of `sys_chars`, and no byte of it outlives the round it
    was fetched for.

    What stays is the two revocations, and BOTH are still needed although
    neither carries data any more:

      * the empty leaf on the FIXED path `memory.recall`. `system.*` is upserted
        per slot path in the brain cell, so a path that is not sent is a path
        that is not TOUCHED: without the leaf, a bundle a previous collector
        wrote there stands in the prompt forever. It is the collector's claim on
        the one path it can name, and the empty text contributes nothing to the
        prompt -- `walk_collect` drops it.
      * the GH #264 marker on `system.memory`. The `json` form named its
        sub-keys PER BUNDLE, so a key written before this wave has no path the
        collector could name empty, and the brain's per-slot upsert would keep
        it in the prompt until something writes that exact path again -- for a
        key derived from what was recalled, possibly never (GH #266).

    Unconditional, and no longer tied to `memory_form` in either half -- which
    is what the old code could not be. With no data in the node there is no
    form whose keys still have to be chosen, so the leaf and the marker are
    both simply always there; an instance retuned from `readable` to `json` (or
    back) would otherwise carry its last leaf or its last keys for the rest of
    its life.

    Stamped in one literal, and `$` stays the substrate's reserved namespace
    inside a system subtree: nothing a memory hive emits can reach this node any
    more, so no bundle key can shadow the marker with data.

    The root is this node and no other. One segment up (`system` itself) the
    root is EMPTY and would revoke every other writer's slot in the brain --
    instructions, handover, the affinity push lane.

    Returns (system slot, capped). The second half is always 0 now: what can be
    capped is the tool result, and `brain_message` caps it where it lives.
    """
    if not MEMORY_TIER:
        return {}, 0
    return {"memory": {"recall": {"text": ""}, "$replace": True}}, 0


def recall_ask(query, tier, tid=None, call_id="", w_from="", w_to=""):
    """The ONE request shape on the recall port. The ambient leg (once per turn)
    and a tool call (GH #78) travel the SAME edge, so every key is always
    present and empty rather than absent -- a missing hop key makes the
    promoting CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge.

    `memory_call_id` is what tells the two answers apart on the way back: empty
    means the ambient leg of a turn, set means the result of a call.

    The window keys are the first PRODUCER of the recall window the memory hive
    has understood since P15 -- derived at the CONSUMER, out of what the model
    asked for, instead of guessed by somebody upstream who cannot know."""
    return {"header": head("recall", "recall", tid,
                           {"recall_query": query, "memory_tier": tier,
                            "memory_call_id": call_id,
                            "recall_window_from": w_from,
                            "recall_window_to": w_to}),
            "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": query}]}


def bundle_text(doc):
    """A recall bundle as ONE tool_result text, in the configured form. The
    collector renders nothing of its own here either -- it concatenates what the
    memory hive emitted. The per-item cap (params.tool_chars) runs at READ
    time, like on every other tool result, so the full bundle stays in the
    round table."""
    readable = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        readable = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    slot = (doc.get("system") or {}).get("memory", {})
    parts = []
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("readable", "both") and readable:
        parts.append(readable)
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("json", "both") and slot:
        parts.append(json.dumps(slot))
    if not parts:
        parts.append(readable or (json.dumps(slot) if slot else
                                  "memory recall returned nothing"))
    return "\n".join(parts)


def recall_call(mem):
    """The synthetic `memory_recall` call the ambient bundle is the answer to
    (GH #278).

    Nobody emitted this call: the collector asks memory before the model has
    seen the turn, which is the whole point of the ambient leg (GH #78). But the
    ANSWER is a tool result whoever asked for it, and a tool result without its
    tool_call is a malformed turn for every provider. So the call is
    reconstructed out of the bundle that came back -- under the name this
    collector already SERVES on `in_memory_call`, so a model that reacts to it
    by calling the tool itself reaches a real edge instead of a void, and
    carrying the question the bundle itself records having been asked with.

    The id is DERIVED, never drawn. `as_of` and the query are what identify one
    recall, and hashing them makes a re-assembly of the same turn -- a tool
    round re-entering the seam, a redelivery, a retry -- the SAME call rather
    than a second question the model has to explain to itself. The two are
    joined by a unit separator: a value that cannot occur in either of them, so
    no pair of (as_of, query) can be spelled two ways.

    TWO SEPARATE READS over the same slot, and that is the point. The IDENTITY
    needs `as_of`, because the query alone repeats across turns. The QUESTION
    does not: a tier-0 bundle carries `query` and no `as_of` at all (it is a
    deterministic projection, not a dated lookup), so gating the query on
    `as_of` too would have sent every tier-0 turn a call that asked nothing.
    An id with no `as_of` to hash falls back to the rendered block, which
    identifies that bundle just as well -- and two turns whose tier-0 bundle
    renders identically then share an id, which is the honest reading: it is
    the same evidence, handed over again.
    """
    slot = (mem.get("system") or {}).get("memory", {})
    raw, query = "", ""
    for key in sorted(slot):
        val = slot.get(key)
        if not isinstance(val, dict) or not isinstance(val.get("text"), str):
            continue
        try:
            b = json.loads(val["text"])
        except Exception:
            continue
        if not isinstance(b, dict):
            continue
        if not query and isinstance(b.get("query"), str):
            query = b["query"]
        if not raw and "as_of" in b:
            raw = "%s\x1f%s" % (b.get("as_of", ""), str(b.get("query", "") or ""))
    if not raw:
        raw = bundle_text(mem)
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
            "id": "call_recall_" + hashlib.sha256(
                raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16],
            "text": json.dumps({"name": "memory_recall",
                                "arguments": json.dumps({"query": query})})}


def memory_result(call_id, text):
    """The answer to a memory_recall call, filed as what it is: a tool result of
    the running round, under the ORIGINAL tool_call_id. Everything after this
    row is the ordinary fan-in -- same phase, same guard, same caps -- so the
    round stays ONE round and memory never learns dispatcher vocabulary."""
    return round_park("tool", {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                              "id": call_id, "text": text}, "round-check")


def thread_result(call_id, text, tid=None):
    """The answer to a `thread_recall` call, filed as what it is: a tool result
    of the running round, under the ORIGINAL tool_call_id. The `tr` marker is
    store bookkeeping -- it is how the next call knows what this turn has
    already spent -- and never reaches the wire."""
    return round_park("tool", {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                              "id": call_id, "text": text, "tr": 1},
                      "round-check", tid=tid, head_tid=tid)


def thread_payload(rows, kind, ref, spent):
    """What a recall hands back: the ORIGINAL rows, out of this turn's own
    slate, UNCAPPED -- that is the entire point, and a recall that re-applies
    the cap it was called to undo is theatre.

    Three ways to name what is wanted, all deterministic and none of them a
    similarity search: a call id (what a stub prints), an iteration number, or a
    plain substring. Nothing here is retrieved by embedding; this is a table
    lookup over rows the cell wrote itself.

    The budget is a WALL, not a cap: over it the call is answered with a typed
    error naming the number, because a recall silently halved is a lie about
    what the model was shown. Returns the text to answer with."""
    cap = (int(CONTEXT_WINDOW * THREAD_RECALL_BUDGET) * 4 if CONTEXT_WINDOW
           else ROUND_BYTES)
    found = []
    for r in rows:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for x in (t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])):
            if not isinstance(x, dict) or x.get("tr") or x.get("lost"):
                continue
            text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
            if kind == "call" and str(x.get("id") or "") != ref:
                continue
            if kind == "round" and str(int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0)) != ref:
                continue
            if kind == "query" and ref.lower() not in text.lower():
                continue
            found.append("[%s iter=%s id=%s]\n%s"
                         % (x.get("type", "?"), r.get("iter", 0),
                            x.get("id", ""), text))
    if not found:
        return "thread recall found nothing for %s=%s in this turn" % (kind, ref)
    payload = "\n\n".join(found)
    if spent + len(payload) > cap:
        return ("thread recall refused: %d characters would exceed this turn's"
                " recall budget of %d (already spent %d). Ask for one call_id"
                " instead of a round or a query."
                % (len(payload), cap, spent))
    return payload


# WHAT AN EVENT LOOKS LIKE ON THE WIRE (GH #540). A provider knows two inbound
# roles and only two: the person's word and the agent's own. An `advice` row is
# neither -- it is the answer this agent's OWN reasoning core handed back on
# `in_advice`, long after the round that asked it ended -- and it used to leave
# this seam as a bare `origin: user` text, byte for byte the shape of a new
# sentence by the person. So the model read it as one. Measured on a live colony,
# one "plan me a thorough three-day trip" turn: the core's plan came back, the
# surface consulted a SECOND time quoting it back as "he supplied the following
# figures, not checked live", and then told the person "Yes. We take the cheap
# option" -- an answer to a question nobody had asked. The plan itself never
# reached the reader.
#
# The role STAYS `user`: it is the only inbound role every provider accepts
# mid-conversation, and what was wrong was never the role on its own but that
# nothing beside it said what the row is. A `tool_result` under the original
# `consult_cogny` call id would be the truer shape and is not available here --
# that call belongs to a round that has ended, so it is not in `messages[]`, and
# a tool result with no preceding call is a provider error rather than a better
# frame. The text frame is provider-neutral, costs one line, and carries the
# correlation id the reply half of the lane needs anyway.
#
# The STORE role is untouched: `advice` stays `advice`, `SAID` still refuses it
# (GH #282), and a batch and a prune still tell an event from a user's word.
ADVICE_FRAME = "[advice from your reasoning core, consult %s]\n%s"
ADVICE_FRAME_ANON = "[advice from your reasoning core]\n%s"

# The other half of the same repair, and the reason it lives HERE. Knowing that
# a row is an advice does not yet say what to do with one; the charter of a
# grown brain is not a place this can be written, because a seed is read once at
# birth and an imported, rebuilt or transferred brain never receives it (the
# failure GH #512 and GH #525 measured twice). A slot this cell re-derives every
# round reaches every talky that stands in front of a core, whatever its birth.
CONSULT_RULE = ("An advice is the answer to YOUR consultation: pass it on to the"
                " person in your own words. Do not consult again about it --"
                " unless the core asks YOU something back, and then you answer the"
                " core, with its consult_id, never the person.")


def wire_turn(t):
    """One window row in the shape a provider reads (GH #540)."""
    role = str(t.get("role") or "")
    text = str(t.get("text", "") or "")
    if role == "assistant":
        return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "text", "text": text}
    if role == "advice":
        cid = str(t.get("consult_id", "") or "")
        text = (ADVICE_FRAME % (cid, text)) if cid else (ADVICE_FRAME_ANON % text)
    return {"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": text}


def brain_message(rows, nxt):
    """The ONE seam. Everything the agent LLM is going to see leaves through
    this message and no other: rolling window, memory bundle, tool round.

    It is also where the round ENDS (GH #77). A turn that has spent its
    iteration budget leaves on the ANSWER lane with everything it collected
    instead of asking the brain again, and says so with round_capped=1. The
    round begins at the seam, so nothing downstream is ever needed to stop it.
    """
    spent = it >= MAX_ITER
    win = leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {"turns": [], "dropped": 0, "capped": 0}
    mem = leg_of(rows, "leg-memory")
    # NOT `SAID` (GH #282): the window is not the memory. Inside the PROMPT an
    # `advice` turn should read as something said -- the agent has to see what
    # the advisor came back with, and the correlation id it carries is the reply
    # half of the bilateral lane. Only what becomes an EPISODE is attributed
    # from the dict; here every turn in the window is shown, and anything that
    # is not the agent's own voice is the other side of the conversation --
    # SAYING WHICH OTHER SIDE IT IS (GH #540, `wire_turn` above).
    msgs = [wire_turn(t) for t in win.get("turns", [])]
    thread, dropped, capped, stale, names, recalled, tp = thread_of(rows)
    msgs.extend(thread)
    sysm, mem_capped = system_of(mem)
    # THE AMBIENT BUNDLE, delivered as the evidence it is (GH #278): the last
    # two entries of the conversation are a `memory_recall` call and its result.
    # It used to enter as `system.memory` and STAY there -- durable state, in
    # the place an agent's instructions live, with nothing saying it was the
    # answer to one question asked once. A model reading a lookup presented as
    # configuration discounts it, and a slot nothing expires goes stale in
    # silence.
    #
    # BEFORE `curate(...)`, and precisely worded: the bundle was never OUTSIDE
    # the budget. `curate` is handed `len(json.dumps(sysm))` and adds it to
    # every projection, so the bytes were always counted -- as an opaque lump
    # nobody could attribute to anything, in a subtree the curator may not
    # touch. Here they are counted as what they are, item by item, in the same
    # list as every other piece of evidence the round produced. The pair is
    # still never a curation CANDIDATE -- curation only touches items tagged
    # with an iteration (`_it`), and this pair belongs to no round -- so a
    # bundle the model was told it has is a bundle it can still read.
    #
    # The same knob caps the same text where the text now is (`memory_chars`),
    # and `hop.memory_capped` keeps its meaning: it is measured on the tool
    # result.
    if MEMORY_TIER and mem:
        call = recall_call(mem)
        text, mem_capped = cap_text(bundle_text(mem))
        msgs.append(call)
        msgs.append({"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                     "id": call["id"], "text": text})
    # The reply half of the bilateral lane (R-CG-3): a model can only pass a
    # correlation id back if it was shown one. The ids of the advice turns
    # STILL IN THE WINDOW travel as data -- no prose, no rendering, and they
    # expire exactly when the window forgets the event they belong to.
    consults = []
    for t in win.get("turns", []):
        cid = str(t.get("consult_id", "") or "")
        if cid and cid not in consults:
            consults.append(cid)
    # The slot travels UNCONDITIONALLY (GH #259). `system.*` is durable state in
    # the brain cell: it is upserted per slot path, so a path that is not sent
    # is a path that is not TOUCHED. A slot that is only ever set therefore
    # keeps naming a consultation that closed long ago -- the promise above
    # ("they expire ... ") is kept by sending the empty rendering, not by
    # falling silent. Durable state is revoked, never merely abandoned.
    #
    # The system tree reaches a provider through `text` leaves only, so the ids
    # get one -- and the emptied slot needs it too: the leaf is what the upsert
    # overwrites, and `{"open": []}` alone would produce no leaf and no write.
    # Three words of label and the raw ids; the collector still renders nothing,
    # it just makes the data readable where it has to be read. The empty text
    # contributes nothing to the prompt, which is the intended "nothing open".
    sysm = dict(sysm)
    sysm["consult"] = {"open": consults,
                       "text": ("open consults: " + ", ".join(consults)
                                + "\n" + CONSULT_RULE
                                if consults else "")}
    # THE ANNOTATION IS ASKED FOR HERE, ON EVERY ASSEMBLY (GH #525). Since
    # `talky@4.1.0` the inline sidecar is the only path from a conversation into
    # new FACTS -- GH #298 removed the batch extractor and GH #379 retracted the
    # tool form -- and the whole lane behind it is inert without the block:
    # "without the extraction prompt the splitter is a pure pass-through".
    # Nothing shipped the block. It lived in a document that asks a reader to
    # paste it into an identity, so a colony ran the splitter, the lane, the
    # ingress and both required drains for weeks with `episodes` growing and
    # `facts` standing still, and every part of it reported healthy.
    #
    # WHY HERE AND NOT IN A SEED. A seed is written once, at birth: a brain that
    # grew -- imported, rebuilt, transferred -- never receives it, and that is
    # exactly the failure GH #512 measured for the two tool declarations. A slot
    # this cell re-derives every round is the only shape that reaches a brain
    # whose birth is behind it.
    #
    # WHY IT IS NOT AN IDENTITY. The block describes a fence a cell of this
    # composite cuts with. Put inside a persona it becomes a mechanism a person
    # is expected to copy by hand, and every charter written without it is a
    # colony that stops remembering with nobody saying so.
    if INLINE_EXTRACTION:
        # THE LEAF NAME IS LOAD-BEARING, and this is the one place it shows.
        # `concat_system_prompt` walks a family's leaves in ALPHABETICAL order,
        # so the name decides where the block stands relative to the charter in
        # `instructions.reply`. `sidecar` sorts after `reply`; `extraction`
        # would have sorted before it, and the block would have arrived in front
        # of the instructions it is supposed to follow. The shipped contract
        # opens by saying the annotation comes AFTER the answer -- a model that
        # produces its structured field before its reasoning answers from
        # nothing, which is the one robust finding in the format-constraint
        # literature -- and an ordering the prose asks for and the assembly
        # reverses is worse than no ordering at all.
        sysm["instructions"] = {"sidecar": {"text": EXTRACTION_CONTRACT}}
    # The curator runs LAST and over the finished projection: it is the only
    # thing here that needs to know how large the whole window is, and the whole
    # window is not knowable before every leg has met.
    #
    # Since GH #451 it is handed the projection ITSELF instead of a number for
    # the half it could not see: the rounds, the window, the `system` tree as a
    # tree, and the tool menu as an array. `sys_chars` used to be
    # `len(json.dumps(sysm))` and the declarations were in NO sum at all --
    # which is how the largest block in a real prompt stayed outside the
    # arithmetic of the component whose whole job is that arithmetic. What may
    # be elided is still narrow and still declared: SYS_KEEP protects every
    # family the collector does not write, and a tool used inside the kept
    # rounds is never a candidate.
    msgs, sysm, tools, cur = curate(msgs, names, recalled, sysm,
                                    list(TOOLS), tp)
    # The menu travels as the subtree the `llm` cell reads, and only when this
    # collector carries one: a tree whose declarations live in its brain must
    # see no `system.tools` write from here, or a curator with an empty menu
    # would revoke the model's entire tool set on its first turn.
    if TOOLS:
        sysm["tools"] = tools_slot(tools)
    out = {"header": head("answer" if spent else "brain", "", extra={
        "iter": str(nxt),
        "window_turns": str(len(win.get("turns", []))),
        "window_dropped": str(win.get("dropped", 0)),
        "window_capped": str(win.get("capped", 0)),
        "round_dropped": str(dropped),
        "round_capped": "1" if (spent or capped) else "0",
        "round_stale": "1" if stale else "0",
        "round_deferred": "1" if win.get("deferred", 0) else "0",
        "memory_capped": str(mem_capped), **cur}),
        "messages": msgs}
    if sysm:
        out["system"] = sysm
    return out


def seam_out(rows, nxt):
    """The seam plus its bookkeeping (GH #103): when deferred turns travel in
    this assembly, their stamp is cleared in the same multi-send --
    round_deferred marks the ARRIVAL at the brain, not every later window that
    still happens to contain the turn."""
    msg = brain_message(rows, nxt)
    out = [msg]
    if msg["header"].get("round_deferred") == "1":
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                             "set": {"deferred": 0},
                             "where": {"session_id": session, "deferred": 1}},
                            "defer-clear"))
    return out


# WHO SAID IT -- the whole answer, with nothing behind it (GH #282). This dict
# is BOTH halves of the question: a role it does not name is not something
# somebody said, so it never becomes an episode, and there is no second name to
# sign one with. `drainable_turns` refuses on it and both writers -- the close
# lane's `close_batch` and the per-turn lane's `turn_episode` -- index into it;
# a role that survived the first can never miss in the second.
#
# It replaces `("assistant" if role == "assistant" else "user")`, which mapped
# EVERY other role to `user` -- including `advice`. That is the row measured in
# #282: `sender=user "Reliably stored are four things: name, editor, city,
# timezone."` The user never said that. It is the hive's own recall, rendered by
# the advisor, handed back on `in_advice` and drained into the memory under the
# user's name -- the loop closes, and the memory starts quoting itself.
SAID = {"user": "user", "assistant": "assistant"}


def drainable_turns(rows):
    """What may leave the write path and become an episode (GH #282).

    Three row classes are measured, and only one of them is something somebody
    said:

    - a TURN -- `role` in `SAID`, the user's word and the agent's own --
      travels;
    - an ADVICE row -- `role = "advice"`, the answer the advisor came back with
      on `in_advice` (R-CG-3) -- stays. It reads like an answer and belongs in
      the context window, because the agent is about to speak in its own voice
      about it; but nobody in this conversation said it, and it is itself a
      rendering of what the memory already holds. Draining it feeds a memory
      its own answers.
    - an INTERIM answer -- `interim = 1`, "one moment, I'm thinking about
      that." (R-CG-3) -- stays. It is an answer on the wire and it belongs in
      the context window, because the model must know it said it; it is not
      something anybody told anybody, and a memory that keeps it keeps filler
      once per deferred turn.

    Everything else stays in the window for the same reason: it is context for
    the model, never an episode. Both writers ask HERE, so what may become a
    memory is decided in one place and stays decidable there. The list is also
    what the per-turn index counts: a row that is not a turn takes no index,
    or the same turn would be written twice under two names.
    """
    return [r for r in rows
            if str(r.get("role") or "") in SAID
            and int(r.get("interim") or 0) == 0]


def close_batch(rows):
    """The session, handed on in ONE message (R-OS-6).

    The window store IS the durable record of the day; a close request only
    asks for it back. messages[] is the conversation in the order it happened,
    `rounds` carries the raw round rows next to it -- the tool rounds AND the
    eviction report of every turn -- parsed but not summarised and not judged.
    Append-all: what is extracted and what is kept belongs to whoever the
    `write` edge leads to, never to the collector.
    """
    turns, rounds = [], []
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("role") == "leg-close":
            try:
                turns = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "[]") or []
            except Exception:
                turns = []
            continue
        row = dict(r)
        try:
            row["turn"] = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            pass
        rounds.append(row)
    msgs = [{"origin": SAID[str(t.get("role") or "")],
             "type": "text", "text": str(t.get("text", "") or "")}
            for t in drainable_turns(turns)]
    return {"header": head("write", "", CLOSE_ID,
                           {"turn_count": str(len(msgs)),
                            "round_count": str(len(rounds))}),
            "messages": msgs, "rounds": rounds}



def day_select(ph):
    """The day so far, in the order it happened. The same read the close lane
    does, and uncapped for the same reason: the knobs above bound a context
    WINDOW, and the index an episode id is minted from counts from the first
    turn of the session -- never from the first turn that still fits in a
    window.

    The projection IS what the phase can decide on: `interim` and `role` are the
    filter, `episode_written` is the idempotence guard, `recorded_at` is the
    event time an episode carries, and a column that is not selected is a column
    that is not there."""
    return store_op(day_call(), ph)


def day_call():
    """The args half of `day_select` -- one definition of the columns, whether
    the read travels alone or as a call of the turn-opening bundle (#419)."""
    return {"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
            "columns": ["id", "role", "content", "interim",
                        "recorded_at", "episode_written"],
            "where": {"session_id": session},
            "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]}


def turn_episode(row, index):
    """ONE turn, on route `turn_write` -- never on `write` (GH #298, Q11).

    The close route has other consumers (a summarizer, an archive); firing it
    per turn would put a model call on a path that is model-free by spec. That
    it is one turn per message is not a preference either: the memory hive's
    writer takes the FIRST user/assistant text turn of a body and ignores the
    rest, so one turn per message is what the port accepts.

    The id is deterministic -- `"<session_id>#<index>"`, the index being the
    row's position among the DRAINABLE turns of the session. It is no longer a
    ledger key (idempotence is `episode_written`); it is kept because a bulk
    import mints exactly this formula and a live session has to name a turn the
    same way, and because a duplicate is only findable in the store if its id
    says which turn it is.

    Nothing here writes a speaker, and that is the point: the episode inherits
    the `context` of the chain it belongs to -- the turn echo belongs to the
    user's message, the answer echo to the answer -- so identity travels per
    message without anybody asserting it in a body."""
    return {"header": head("turn_write", "", session + "#" + str(index),
                           {"turn_index": str(index),
                            "happened_at": str(row.get("recorded_at") or "")}),
            "messages": [{"origin": SAID[str(row.get("role") or "")],
                          "type": "text", "text": str(row.get("content") or "")}]}


# ==================================================================== LANES
# Lanes are read BEFORE phases: a message that arrives over a port edge carries
# whatever col_phase the chain happened to leave in its context, and the lane is
# the only thing that says what it IS.

# THE DOOR IN THE WALL (GH #458). `talky` and `cogny` are sealed hives: an edge
# naming their `./brain` is refused with `hive_port_boundary`, and the only way
# from outside to the brain runs through this cell. So until now no shipped
# agent had an entrance for its own identity at all -- `affinity` could push,
# and there was nowhere to push to.
#
# It is a lane of its own and not a body flag, for the reason the `in_tool` lane
# below already gives at length: what leaves this seam in `system.*` is UPSERTed
# into the brain's own cell.db and stands there until something overwrites that
# exact path. That is durable state of the agent. It is right for an identity
# and wrong for a tool result, and telling the two apart by the LANE means the
# distinction is drawn by the topology -- by an edge the colony wrote -- rather
# than by a key in a body that a model could have written.
#
# TWO SHAPES, ONE MEANING. `system` is what an `llm` cell upserts and what
# `affinity`'s push lane already emits: the slots and no turn beside them, so
# the update costs a write and not an inference (GH #263). `slot`/`content` is
# the same thing for a single slot, for a caller writing one pack by hand. A
# message may carry both; the single slot is merged over the tree.
#
# ALL OR NOTHING. An unknown slot refuses the WHOLE pack. Writing the half that
# was understood would leave the sender an `ok` it cannot tell apart from a
# complete write, and a half-written identity is worse than none -- the same
# reason the substrate delivers a message whose pointers would not all resolve
# not at all rather than half-expanded (CLAUDE.md, invariant 14).
if lane == "in_pack":
    pack = d.get("system")
    pack = dict(pack) if isinstance(pack, dict) else {}
    one = str(d.get("slot") or "")
    if one:
        pack[one] = d.get("content")
    # The owner comes off the ENVELOPE and never out of the body. A cell knows
    # no sender, and the only trustworthy origin in this substrate is what the
    # substrate itself wrote -- the same rule `affinity`'s gate states for
    # `context.actor` and the `display` hive states for a view's owner.
    owner = str(envelope.get("reply_to") or "")
    named = ",".join(sorted(pack))
    bad = sorted(k for k in pack if k not in PACK_SLOTS)
    code = ""
    if not pack:
        # An empty pack is a refusal and not a no-op: a sender that meant to
        # write something and addressed the wrong body key must not read
        # silence as success.
        code = "pack_empty"
    elif bad:
        code = "slot_unknown"
    ack = {"pack_owner": owner, "pack_slots": named, "error_code": code,
           "pack_unknown": ",".join(bad)}
    out = []
    if not code:
        # No `messages[]` beside the slots, deliberately: an `llm` cell handed a
        # body with no turn in it upserts and returns without calling, so an
        # identity that changed costs the agent a write and never an inference.
