        out.append({"header": head("pack", "", "", {"pack_owner": owner}),
                    "system": pack})
    out.append({"header": head("pack_ack", "", "", ack),
                "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "text",
                              "text": "pack " + (code or "accepted") + ": "
                                      + (named or "-")}]})
    emit(out)

# THE MENU IS ASKED FOR, NOT TYPED (GH #464). Two lanes and one round trip, and
# they are the same shape as the pack above for the same reason: what comes back
# is DURABLE state of the agent. It travels its own lane, it lands in `system.*`,
# and an `llm` cell upserts it per slot path into its own `cell.db`, where it
# stands until something overwrites that exact path.
#
# WHY IT IS NOT A PER-TURN COST. The tools hive answers questions and raises
# nothing of its own, so somebody has to ask -- and asking in front of every
# assembly would buy a menu nobody typed at the price of a round trip per turn.
# The tick asks, the answer is written once, and every turn after it reads a slot
# that is already in the brain.
#
# WHY IT IS A TICK AND NOT A BIRTH. The substrate hands a cell no message at
# spawn, so the first ask is the first tick rather than the boot itself. That is
# the honest form, and it is also the useful one: a tool ADDED to the hive by
# mutation reaches this agent at the next tick, and nothing over there had to
# push -- which is exactly what the hive's own contract says about asking again.
if lane == "in_menu_tick":
    if not TOOLS_DECLARED or TOOL_MENU:
        park()
    emit([{"header": head("schemas", "", "",
                          {"asked_count": str(len(TOOLS_DECLARED))}),
           "tools": list(TOOLS_DECLARED), "messages": []}])

if lane == "in_menu":
    schemas = [x for x in (d.get("schemas") or []) if isinstance(x, dict)]
    unknown = [str(n) for n in (d.get("unknown") or []) if isinstance(n, str)]
    menu = [provider_tool_of(x) for x in schemas if str(x.get("name") or "")]
    if not menu:
        # An empty menu is never WRITTEN, and since GH #529 it is never
        # RECORDED either. `tools_slot` replaces the whole subtree, so a write
        # here would revoke the model's entire tool set on the strength of an
        # answer that found nothing -- and overwriting this answerer's stored
        # half with an empty one would do the same thing one tick later. The
        # other answerers' halves stand untouched.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: the schemas answer carried no declaration"
                         " this collector could use%s\n"
                         % ((" -- nothing under: " + ", ".join(unknown))
                            if unknown else ""))
        park()
    # THE MENU IS A UNION, AND THE UNION NEEDS A MEMORY (GH #529). Before it,
    # one answer WAS the menu: parse, add the self-served names, write the lot
    # with `$replace`. That is right while exactly one thing answers and is the
    # whole defect the moment two do -- the second answer would not merge with
    # the first, it would delete it, and the two would take the menu away from
    # each other on every tick forever.
    #
    # So each answerer's last submenu is kept as one row of this hive's own
    # store, keyed by WHO delivered it, and the menu is re-derived from all the
    # rows on every answer. Delete-then-insert rather than an update, because
    # the store has no upsert and a first answer has no row to update; the
    # select rides in the same bundle, so it runs over the same connection
    # AFTER the write and sees it (GH #419). Two answerers replying at the same
    # time therefore converge: whichever bundle runs second sees both rows and
    # writes the full union.
    #
    # `unknown` travels with the row instead of being reported here: a name one
    # answerer has nothing under may be a name ANOTHER one delivers, and
    # reporting per answer would make every tick of a two-answerer tree warn
    # about the half of the menu it did not ask this answerer for.
    emit([cstore_bundle(
        [("c-menu-del", {"operation": "delete", "table": "menu",
                         "where": {"answerer": answerer}}),
         ("c-menu-put", {"operation": "insert", "table": "menu",
                         "row": {"answerer": answerer, "tools": menu,
                                 "unknown": ",".join(unknown),
                                 "recorded_at": now}}),
         ("c-menu-all", {"operation": "select", "table": "menu",
                         "columns": ["answerer", "tools", "unknown"]})],
        "menu-merge")])
if lane in ("in_turn", "in_advice"):
    # ONE chain, two occasions. `in_advice` is the return lane of the advisor
    # split (R-CG-3): the advisor's result -- or the question it asks back --
    # arrives long after the turn that asked ended with its interim answer, so
    # it cannot re-enter that round. It is assembled like a TURN and opens a
    # fresh one, which is what makes the follow-up reach the channel in the
    # agent's own voice instead of as a raw advisor reply.
    if op is not None or phase in ("turn-open", "collect", "round-check"):
        park()
    advice = lane == "in_advice"
    tid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    # An event carries the role of ITS conversation, so its text is read
    # without one; the row keeps `advice` as its own role, which is neither the
    # user's word nor the agent's own.
    query = any_text(d) if advice else (text_of(d, "user") or any_text(d))
    # GH #419: the row, the open-round check and the window in ONE message. The
    # insert is in FRONT of the window read in the same bundle, so the window
    # contains this very turn -- exactly as it did when the two were two
    # messages, and for the same reason: a bundle's ops run in order over the
    # store's one connection.
    calls = [("c-open-turn",
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
               "row": {"id": now + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "session_id": session,
                       "turn_id": tid, "role": "advice" if advice else "user",
                       "content": query, "recorded_at": now, "deferred": 0,
                       "consult_id": consult if advice else ""}}),
             # Since GH #103 the chain first asks whether a tool round of the
             # session is still open -- an assistant row whose guard has not
             # fired -- because a mid-round turn defers instead of assembling.
             ("c-open-round",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
               "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "recorded_at", "session_id"],
               "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}),
             # The window, read UNCONDITIONALLY. A deferring turn throws it
             # away, which costs one read of at most WINDOW_TURNS rows -- and
             # buys the two messages the turn-open/win chain used to cost. The
             # decision stays in code, where it always was.
             ("c-open-win",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
               "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "role", "content",
                           "recorded_at", "deferred", "consult_id"],
               "where": {"session_id": session},
               "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "desc"}],
               "limit": WINDOW_TURNS})]
    if TURN_WRITE not in ("", "0"):
        # Next to the machine, never inside it: the round check keeps deciding
        # what happens to this turn, and the per-turn write is a second lane
        # that cannot affect it.
        calls.append(("c-open-day", day_call()))
    out = [cstore_bundle(calls, "turn-open", tid)]
    if MEMORY_TIER:
        # Asked HERE, once per turn, because the collector is the place that
        # decides what enters the context window. The ambient ask carries no
        # call id and no window: it is the free floor under every turn, and the
        # model has not seen the turn yet when it leaves (GH #78).
        out.append(recall_ask(query, MEMORY_TIER, tid))
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_bundle":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    # ONE port, two meanings, told apart by the correlation key the request
    # carried out (GH #78): a bundle with a call id answers a `memory_recall`
    # tool_call and is therefore a RESULT of the running round; a bundle
    # without one is the ambient leg of the turn.
    call_id = str(ctx.get("memory_call_id", "") or "")
    if call_id:
        emit([memory_result(call_id, bundle_text(d))])
    emit([round_park("leg-memory", {"system": d.get("system", {}),
                                   "messages": d.get("messages", [])}, "collect", 0)])

if lane == "in_calls":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    # The async class, as the dispatcher classified it (R-CG-3, delta 2). Those
    # ids are NOT part of the expectation set: they are acknowledged on the
    # spot, under their own tool_call_id, so the assistant turn stays
    # well-formed for every provider. And when nothing else was asked and the
    # turn is over anyway (see below), the row is filed as ALREADY fired -- no
    # guard to win, no open round for a sweep to find, and therefore no idle
    # window racing an advisor's thinking time.
    async_ids = [x for x in str(hop.get("async_calls", "") or "").split(",") if x]
    # The HANDOFF subset of the same classification (GH #372): the calls whose
    # lane also takes the TURN over. Declared at the dispatcher like the async
    # class itself and obeyed here -- which of the two a tool is, is tool
    # semantics, and this cell classifies nothing.
    handoff_ids = [x for x in str(hop.get("handoff_calls", "") or "").split(",") if x]
    # The one number in the whole system that is not an estimate: what the
    # PROVIDER counted for the prompt it just answered. It reaches this cell
    # only when nothing in between dropped the key, so it is stored when it is
    # there and never waited for -- a curator that stops working because a
    # provider omitted a usage field is the goose bug (hard-coded 128K), and it
    # fires four times too early.
    try:
        tp = int(hop.get("tokens_prompt") or 0)
    except Exception:
        tp = 0
    if tp:
        msgs = [dict(m, tp=tp) if m.get("type") == "tool_call" else m for m in msgs]
    ids = [str(m.get("id") or "") for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]
    acked = [i for i in ids if i in async_ids]
    waiting = [i for i in ids if i not in async_ids]
    # WHAT ENDS A ROUND IS AN ANSWER (GH #372), and there are exactly two ways an
    # async-only bundle can have one. Filing the row as already fired ends the
    # round on the spot, which is honest only if this turn is going to be
    # answered by somebody:
    #
    #   * the model spoke beside the bundle -- the dispatcher already sent that
    #     sentence to the channel as the interim answer (it sends one only when
    #     there IS text, which is why this reads the turns the same way it does,
    #     one condition in two cells rather than two spellings of it); or
    #   * a HANDOFF call took the turn with it -- an advisor's event, an
    #     escalation re-entering the seam: the answer comes from a later turn.
    #
    # Neither, and the round is NOT over: the model has not answered yet. The
    # acknowledgements below complete the fan-in, the REGULAR guard fires, and
    # the seam re-enters the brain with everything the round collected. No new
    # route and no new sort -- the re-entry is bounded by params.max_iter like
    # every other round, and a spent budget leaves the same seam on 'answer'
    # with round_capped=1.
    #
    # Measured before the fix: a bare `remember` call -- fire-and-forget, async
    # but no handoff -- filed the round as fired and the channel got NOTHING. No
    # interim, no final, no error, and `round_idle_ms` does not fire on a quiet
    # channel. Three of five full harness runs died that way, and the per-turn
    # contract (GH #298) makes call-only iterations common.
    handed = [i for i in acked if i in handoff_ids]
    said = any(m.get("type") in ("text", None) and str(m.get("text", "") or "")
               for m in msgs)
    over = bool(said or handed)
    out = [round_park("assistant", msgs, "round-check",
                      fired=1 if acked and not waiting and over else 0)]
    out.extend(round_park("tool",
                          {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": i,
                           "text": "handed to the async lane: this answer"
                                   " arrives later as its own event"},
                          "round-check") for i in acked)
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_tool":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    # WHAT A TOOL RESULT MAY CARRY (GH #252): its `messages[]` -- all of it, in
    # the order the tool wrote it -- and nothing else. Every turn is filed under
    # the `id` of the call it answers, because that correlation is the only one
    # a round has and the only one a provider has. This used to read `msgs[0]`,
    # so a tool that answered two calls in ONE message closed one of them and
    # left the other waiting for the idle sweep.
    #
    # The `system` slot of a tool result is deliberately NOT kept, and the
    # `in_bundle` lane above is not the precedent it looks like. `system.*` that
    # leaves this seam is UPSERTed into the brain cell's own cell.db and stays
    # there until something overwrites that exact slot path: it is DURABLE state
    # of the agent, not evidence of one round. A tool result gets no second
    # chance to correct itself, and a brief about one subject would still stand
    # in the prompt three subjects later. `system.*` is also out of the
    # curator's reach on purpose -- it is where hard constraints belong -- so a
    # tool writing there would grow the prompt with nothing left able to cut it.
    # A tool with something to say says it in the text of its result.
    #
    # RETRACTED with GH #278. This used to carve out one payload: the recall
    # bundle, it said, MAY live there because it is re-sent under a FIXED path
    # on every single turn and can therefore never go stale. It does not live
    # there any more. A durable slot is discounted by the model, goes stale the
    # first turn that does not re-send it, and lies outside the curator's reach
    # -- its bytes were always counted, but only as an anonymous lump of
    # sys_chars no stage could attribute. The bundle travels as the
    # `memory_recall` tool result of its own round now (`system_of`,
    # `recall_call`), which leaves the rule above without an exception.
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    # One turn stays a dict, which is the row shape every store already holds;
    # several travel as the list `thread_of` and `round_sets` both read.
    emit([round_park("tool", msgs[0] if len(msgs) == 1 else msgs, "round-check")])

if lane == "in_memory_call":
    # The memory tool (GH #78). From the dispatcher's side this is a tool like
    # any other -- it names the tool, an edge knows the cell -- and here the
    # cell is the collector itself, because it is the memory specialist of this
    # hive: it already holds the recall port for the per-turn leg. So the call
    # is served HERE and its answer re-enters the fan-in HERE; the round ends
    # in the collector and the dispatcher only ever routed (R-OS-2).
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    call = msgs[0] if msgs else {}
    # The id comes from the TURN, which is also where the round's expectation
    # set came from -- one source, or the two could disagree and the fan-in
    # would wait for a call nobody can answer.
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "")
    if not call_id:
        park()
    try:
        args = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        args = {}
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        args = {}
    query = str(args.get("query", "") or "")
    if not MEMORY_CALL_TIER:
        # Switched off. A call that cannot be served is ANSWERED, not parked:
        # asking into a port that is not there would hang the fan-in until the
        # idle exit. Same lid pattern as the dispatcher's budget refusal.
        emit([memory_result(call_id, "memory recall is not configured"
                                     " in this collector")])
    # The window arguments travel as the recall port's own keys. What the model
    # did not name stays empty, and an empty window is a point query -- the
    # memory hive's own default, not a decision taken here.
    emit([recall_ask(query, MEMORY_CALL_TIER, None, call_id,
                     str(args.get("window_from", "") or ""),
                     str(args.get("window_to", "") or ""))])

if lane == "in_thread_call":
    # The thread tool (B5). Same bauform as the memory tool one lane up, and
    # for the same reason: the collector owns the slate a stub points at, so
    # the collector serves the call itself and the round ends where it began
    # (R-OS-2). The difference is the archive -- `memory_recall` asks the hive
    # about the past, `thread_recall` asks THIS TURN's own round table about a
    # payload the curator elided ten minutes ago. Without it every stub is a
    # dead end, and a dead end is worse than no stub at all.
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    call = msgs[0] if msgs else {}
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "")
    if not call_id:
        park()
    try:
        args = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        args = {}
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        args = {}
    if not THREAD_RECALL:
        emit([thread_result(call_id, "thread recall is not configured"
                                     " in this collector")])
    # A `tool:<name>` key names a DECLARATION stage 4 stubbed, not a payload of
    # this round -- so it is answered right here, out of the menu this cell
    # already holds, with no store read and no budget wall. The stub the model
    # is reading printed exactly this key, and a schema is small.
    want = str(args.get("call_id", "") or "")
    if want.startswith("tool:"):
        emit([thread_result(call_id, tool_schema_text(want[5:]), tid=None)])
    kind, ref = "call", want
    if not ref and str(args.get("round", "") or ""):
        kind, ref = "round", str(args.get("round"))
    if not ref:
        kind, ref = "query", str(args.get("query", "") or "")
    if not ref:
        emit([thread_result(call_id, "thread recall needs one of call_id,"
                                     " round or query")])
    # The chain state rides in the hop id, like the prune chain (GH #76): this
    # script keeps no state between hops, and the internal hive edge promotes
    # nothing but the context keys. The real turn id is the first field and is
    # split back out on the other side.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"turn_id": turn_id}},
                   "tr-sel", "|".join([turn_id, call_id, kind, ref]))])

if lane == "in_answer":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    answer = text_of(d, "assistant")
    # An interim answer is an answer -- it enters the window like any other and
    # leaves on the same lane -- but it says so, so a channel can render "one
    # moment" differently from the real reply (R-CG-3). ONE condition, two
    # places: the wire marker tells a channel, the stored column tells the write
    # path (GH #282). Until the column existed the marker lived on the wire
    # alone, and "one moment, I'm thinking about that." became an episode.
    is_interim = str(hop.get("interim", "")) == "1"
    mark = {"interim": "1"} if is_interim else None
    out = [store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
                     "row": {"id": now + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "session_id": session,
                             "turn_id": turn_id, "role": "assistant", "content": answer,
                             "recorded_at": now, "deferred": 0,
                             "interim": 1 if is_interim else 0}}, "ans-w"),
           {"header": head("answer", extra=mark), "messages": d.get("messages", [])}]
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_close":
    # The session keeper says a generation is over; the collector answers with
    # the generation. Uncapped by design: the knobs above bound a CONTEXT
    # window, and this is the durable record leaving, not a prompt. The hop id
    # carries the ARRIVAL time as the prune boundary (GH #76): every turn this
    # cell processed before the close is in the batch (one actor, ordered
    # mailbox), every later one is stamped younger and survives a prune.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
                    "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "role", "content",
                                "recorded_at", "interim"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]},
                   "close-turns", CLOSE_ID + "|" + now)])

if lane == "in_round_sweep":
    # The re-check occasion a parent tree provides (GH #103): a timer or an
    # operator asks whether any round is stuck. The template never fires this
    # itself -- no schedule of its own, the session-keeper discipline. The
    # question is session-agnostic on purpose: a timer knows no session; the
    # rows carry theirs.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "session_id", "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}, "sweep")])

if lane == "in_prune":
    # The operator lane of GH #76. The collector never fires this itself; a
    # parent tree wires a timer or an operator to it. The request reads the
    # delivery ledger -- what may fall follows from evidence, never from age
    # alone, and evidence already used (pruned_at) is not asked again.
    cut = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
           - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=PRUNE_AFTER_MS)).strftime(FMT)
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "batched",
                    "columns": ["session_id", "batched_at"],
                    "where": {"batched_at": {"lte": cut},
                              "pruned_at": {"is_null": True}}},
                   "prune-ledger")])

if lane in LANES:
    park()

# ==================================================== THE STORE SAID NO (#343)
# Since GH #331 every store error path stamps `hop.operation` with the refused
# op, so a refusal arrives looking exactly like an answer: the same phase in the
# context, the same op in the hop. Read as an answer it becomes `json.loads`
# over an error sentence, an empty row list, or -- worst -- a phase that
# advances on a read that never happened. `operation` says WHICH op answered,
# `error_code` says WHETHER it worked, and this cell reads both (the shape
# `builder-librarian/retrieve` was hardened into for GH #308).
#
# `op` is what says "this came from the store": nothing else that reaches this
# cell stamps it (the same discriminator the echo guards already use). So a hop
# carrying BOTH op and error_code is a store refusal, and a refusal is TERMINAL
# -- the chain stops here, no further store op leaves, and the failure is SAID.
#
# Measured before the fix: a refused window read wrote an EMPTY window leg into
# the round table, after which the turn fired and the model answered with no
# conversation at all -- and nobody learned. The report goes out on a lane the
# parent already drains: the prune chain has its own report lane (the one its
# zero-report already uses), every other phase reports where the turn was going
# anyway.
# GH #295: a BUNDLE reply never stamps `error_code` on the hop -- that header
# means "the whole reply is a refusal and carries no payload", and a bundle whose
# second leg failed still hands back the first leg's rows. It stamps
# `bundle_errors` instead, and here one refused leg is one too many: an assembly
# that fires on a half-read round is exactly the "answered with no conversation
# at all" failure #343 exists to prevent. WHICH leg failed is in `results[]`.
bundle_errors = int(hop.get("bundle_errors", 0) or 0)
if bundle_errors and not err:
    for _r in d.get("results") or []:
        if isinstance(_r, dict) and _r.get("error_code"):
            err = str(_r.get("error_code"))
            op = str(_r.get("operation") or op or "")
            break

if err and op and phase.startswith("menu"):
    # A menu is durable state and no turn travels beside it, so a store that
    # refuses one has nothing to report INTO the conversation: the `answer`
    # report below would put "context assembly stopped" in front of a person
    # who asked nothing. It is a warn line and a stop, and the next tick asks
    # again -- which is the whole reason the ask is a tick (GH #529).
    sys.stderr.write("collector: the menu merge stopped in phase '%s': the store"
                     " refused the %s with %s\n" % (phase, op, err))
    park()

if err and op:
    reporting = "prune" if phase.startswith("prune") else "answer"
    marks = {"store_error": err, "store_operation": str(op), "degraded": "1"}
    if reporting == "prune":
        marks.update({"pruned_turns": "0", "pruned_rounds": "0",
                      "prune_boundary": ""})
    emit([{"header": head(reporting, "", extra=marks),
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "context assembly stopped in phase '%s': the store"
                                 " refused the %s with %s (%s)"
                                 % (phase, op, err, any_text(d))}]}])


# ================================================== THE MENU, MERGED (GH #529)
# Every answerer's last submenu, in one place, written with `$replace` exactly
# as one answer used to be. What is new is only WHOSE declarations the replaced
# subtree holds: all of them, plus the names this cell answers itself.
if phase == "menu-merge" and op == "bundle" and not err:
    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-menu-all")
    menu, seen = [], set()
    # Deterministic by ANSWERER name, so the same rows produce the same menu in
    # the same order on every tick and a re-derivation is not a diff. A name two
    # answerers both declare is taken from the first of them: a menu that
    # declared one tool twice is a menu no provider accepts, and which of the
    # two won has to be decided by something a reader can predict.
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("answerer") or "")):
        tools = r.get("tools")
        if isinstance(tools, str):
            try:
                tools = json.loads(tools)
            except Exception:
                tools = []
        for t in (tools if isinstance(tools, list) else []):
            name = tool_name_of(t)
            if name and name not in seen:
                seen.add(name)
                menu.append(t)
    if not menu:
        # The same guard as on the way in, on the other side of the round trip:
        # nothing recorded means nothing to write, and an empty `$replace` is a
        # revocation of the model's whole tool set.
        park()
    # AFTER that guard and never instead of it (GH #512): the names this cell
    # answers itself are not evidence that anybody answered, and a menu carrying
    # nothing but them would still be the revocation the guard exists to refuse.
    # A name an answerer DID deliver wins -- a parent that wired a real cell of
    # its own behind that name has overridden this one.
    mine = [t for t in self_tool_menu() if tool_name_of(t) not in seen]
    for t in mine:
        seen.add(tool_name_of(t))
    menu = menu + mine
    # UNKNOWN, against the MERGED menu (GH #529). A name is a finding only if
    # NOBODY delivered it -- not if the answerer that was asked had nothing
    # under it. That is what makes one declared list askable of several
    # answerers at once: the surface names `consult_cogny` beside its search
    # tools, the tool hive has nothing under the first and the core has nothing
    # under the other two, and neither of those is a defect.
    unknown = []
    for r in rows:
        for name in str(r.get("unknown") or "").split(","):
            name = name.strip()
            if name and name not in seen and name not in unknown:
                unknown.append(name)
    if unknown:
        # NAMED, never dropped. A name nobody has is a declaration in THIS
        # agent's template pointing at nothing, and the whole value of declaring
        # is that somebody can see the declaration was wrong. A `code` cell's
        # stderr lands in `log.jsonl` at warn level and stamps `had_stderr` on
        # the emission, so the line is a receipt a reader finds without opening
        # a body -- and `hop.menu_unknown` carries the same names on the
        # message itself.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: no answerer has a declaration for: %s\n"
                         % ", ".join(unknown))
    emit([{"header": head("menu", "", "",
                          {"menu_count": str(len(menu)),
                           "menu_self": ",".join(tool_name_of(t) for t in mine),
                           "menu_answerers": ",".join(
                               sorted(str(r.get("answerer") or "") for r in rows)),
                           "menu_unknown": ",".join(unknown)}),
           "system": {"tools": tools_slot(menu)}}])

# =================================================================== PHASES
# First assembly of a turn: window leg + optional memory leg, fanned in over
# the round table, fired exactly once by the guarded update. Since GH #103 the
# chain first asks whether a tool round of the session is still open -- an
# assistant row whose guard has not fired -- because a mid-round turn defers
# instead of assembling.
# GH #419: `turn-w`, `turn-open` and `win` were three messages for one question
# -- may this turn be assembled, and out of which window. They are one now, and
# the per-turn scan rides in the same reply.

# The other occasion: the answer is a turn of the day like any other, and it is
# the one a question about the last exchange needs. Its insert echo was a dead
# end until this lane existed.
if phase == "ans-w" and op == "insert" and not err:
    if TURN_WRITE in ("", "0"):
        park()
    emit([day_select("tw-scan")])

def scan_out(rows):
    # One message per unwritten turn, each with the guarded mark that says it
    # left, all in ONE multi-send: what left and what says it left are one
    # emission, never two decisions.
    #
    # Deliberately not "the newest row": with two turns in flight the newest is
    # the wrong one and the other is lost -- the bug the drain's high-water mark
    # existed to prevent. `episode_written` prevents it per ROW instead, and the
    # guard (`where` on the row id AND the column) makes a lost race terminal
    # rather than a second episode.
    out, marks = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(drainable_turns(rows)):
        if int(r.get("episode_written") or 0):
            continue
        out.append(turn_episode(r, i))
        # `or_null`, not a plain 0, and the reason is broader than a migration:
        # NO insert of this cell names the column. It arrives by ALTER TABLE ADD
        # COLUMN, SQLite fills no default, and neither the turn insert nor the
        # answer insert writes it -- so EVERY row reads NULL until this guard
        # sets it, and NULL is not 0. A guard comparing to 0 alone would match
        # no row at all, and the scan would hand every turn out again on every
        # single occasion. NULL means "not written", the read side says the same
        # (`int(... or 0)`), and both sides say it once.
        marks.append(("c-tw-mark-%d" % i,
                      {"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                       "set": {"episode_written": 1},
                       "where": {"id": str(r.get("id") or ""),
                                 "episode_written": {"or_null": {"eq": 0}}}}))
    if len(marks) == 1:
        # A bundle is TWO OR MORE tool_calls (store `tool_call_turn_count`), so a
        # scan that hands out ONE episode marks it with an ordinary single-op
        # update -- the same op, the same guard, the same message count.
        out.append(store_op(marks[0][1], "tw-mark"))
    elif marks:
        # GH #419: N marks, ONE message. The guard stays per ROW (`where` on the
        # id AND the column), so a lost race is still terminal rather than a
        # second episode -- the bundle changes how many messages that costs, not
        # what it guards.
        out.append(cstore_bundle(marks, "tw-mark"))
    return out


if phase == "tw-scan" and op == "select" and not err:
    # The OTHER occasion: the answer turn's own scan, which arrives on its own
    # because the answer is written on its own (`ans-w`).
    out = scan_out(rows_of(d))
    if not out:
        # A session with nothing unwritten in it is not an empty batch, it is
        # nothing -- and a re-delivered scan is a skip, not a second episode.
        park()
    emit(out)

if phase == "turn-open" and op == "bundle":
    out = []
    # The per-turn scan, out of the same reply. It is a SECOND lane and decides
    # nothing about this turn -- so it is collected first and travels with
    # whatever the round check decides below.
    if "c-open-day" in results_by_id(d):
        out.extend(scan_out(bundle_rows_of(d, "c-open-day")))
    # Open rounds the policy can date. An undatable open row predates #103 and
    # must neither be closed nor block the session forever: such a session
    # keeps the pre-#103 behaviour and assembles normally.
    open_rounds = [r for r in bundle_rows_of(d, "c-open-round")
                   if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")]
    if not open_rounds:
        emit(out + [round_park("leg-window",
                               window_of(bundle_rows_of(d, "c-open-win")),
                               "collect", 0)])
    # Mid-round user turn (GH #103): the turn is in the window already and
    # stays there, but it starts NO second assembly while a round of the
    # session is open -- at most ONE open brain call per session, the
    # telephone model (R-OS-3): you answer when the sentence is finished. The
    # stamp is what the next regular assembly reports as round_deferred=1.
    out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                         "set": {"deferred": 1},
                         "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "user"}},
                        "defer-w", extra={"round_deferred": "1"}))
    for r in open_rounds:
        if str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT:
            # The parked arrival is itself the next OCCASION: a round whose
            # start lies behind the idle window gets its re-check, and the
            # regular round-check decides on full progress (GH #103).
            out.append(re_check(r))
    emit(out)

if phase == "collect" and op == "bundle":
    # GH #419 -- the election, without the guard. The window leg parks and the
    # round table is read back in the SAME message: the store runs a bundle's ops
    # in order over its one connection, so the trailing select sees the insert in
    # front of it and of two legs parking concurrently exactly ONE reads a
    # complete set. That is what `gate` (a select), `fire-guard` (a guarded
    # update) and `fire` (a second select) cost, three messages, for a decision a
    # bundle makes for free.
    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-collect-read")
    roles = {r.get("role") for r in rows}
    if not set(EXPECT) <= roles:
        park()
    if len([r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "leg-window"]) > 1:
        # A redelivered leg is a duplicate, not a complete set: firing on it
        # would assemble the same turn twice.
        sys.stderr.write("collector: the window leg parked twice for %s\n" % turn_id)
        park()
    # The `fired` mark of the window leg, and it is the HALF of the old guard
    # that had to stay. `update ... where fired=0` did two jobs: it elected among
    # the legs racing to complete the round (the read-back does that now, for
    # free), and it made the election permanent -- a leg that lands AFTER the
    # turn has left reads a complete set too, and would assemble it a second
    # time. Only the first job went with GH #419.
    if any(int(r.get("fired") or 0) for r in rows if r.get("role") == "leg-window"):
        park()
    emit(seam_out(rows, 0)
         + [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round", "set": {"fired": 1},
                      "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "leg-window", "fired": 0}},
                     "collect-done")])

# Tool round: the fan-in of the store-backed tool loop, now re-entering through
# the same seam and therefore carrying the window and the bundle with it.
if phase in ("round-done", "collect-done") and op == "update":
    # The echo of the closing mark. Nothing follows it -- the seam left with it,
    # in the same multi-send -- and a chain that read this as an occasion would
    # assemble the turn a second time.
    park()

if phase == "sweep" and op == "select" and not err:
    # One re-check per stale open round, all rounds in parallel. Fresh rounds
    # wait, undatable rows keep their pre-#103 behaviour. A sweep that finds
    # nothing stale emits nothing: its observable effect is the round it
    # fires -- this lane is an occasion, not a report lane (the prune lane's
    # heartbeat, R-P5, stays the prune lane's).
    emit([re_check(r) for r in rows_of(d)
          if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
          and str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT])

if phase == "tr-sel" and op == "select" and not err:
    # The other half of the thread tool: the slate came back, the answer is
    # written as an ordinary tool result of the running round -- same phase,
    # same guard, same fan-in. The round table never learns tool vocabulary and
    # the tool never learns store vocabulary.
    parts = turn_id.split("|", 3)
    if len(parts) != 4:
        park()
    tid, call_id, kind, ref = parts
    rows = rows_of(d)
    spent = 0
    for r in rows:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for x in (t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])):
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("tr"):
                spent += len(str(x.get("text", "") or ""))
    emit([thread_result(call_id, thread_payload(rows, kind, ref, spent), tid)])

if phase == "round-check" and op in ("bundle", "select"):
    # `re_check` (GH #103) asks the same question with a bare select: it names a
    # round worth looking at and parks nothing of its own. A bundle is TWO OR
    # MORE tool_calls (store `tool_call_turn_count`), so the two shapes are told
    # apart by the op and read out of the place each one puts its rows.
    # The same cure for the tool round (GH #419): a result parks and reads the
    # slate back in ONE message. `round_sets`, the idle exit and the IDLE_CUT
    # comparison are word for word what `round-check` ran -- only the row source
    # and the election changed.
    rows = bundle_rows_of(d, "c-round-check-read") if op == "bundle" else rows_of(d)
    # Same argument as at the assembly: the mark makes the election permanent.
    # A tool result that arrives after its round has answered -- the advisor's
    # late event is the ordinary case -- reads a complete set too, and without
    # this it would send the turn to the brain a second time.
    if any(int(r.get("fired") or 0) for r in rows
           if r.get("role") == "assistant" and int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) == it):
        park()
    expected, received, progress = round_sets(rows, it)
    missing = expected - received
    if expected and not missing:
        # The `fired` mark stays, and it is NOT the guard it used to be. It says
        # the round is CLOSED (GH #103): `turn-open` reads it to decide whether a
        # mid-round turn defers, and the idle sweep reads it to decide what is
        # still worth re-checking. Both would otherwise keep finding a round that
        # has long since answered. What went with GH #419 is only its
        # `rows_affected` -- the election is the read-back above, and the mark
        # therefore travels WITH the seam instead of one hop in front of it.
        emit(seam_out(rows, it + 1)
             + [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round",
                          "set": {"fired": 1},
                          "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "iter": it,
                                    "role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}, "round-done")])
    if expected and missing and progress and progress < IDLE_CUT:
        # The deterministic exit of GH #103: the round went idle with calls
        # still open, and a message reached this cell anyway. The stand-ins
        # complete the fan-in; everything after this is the regular machine.
        emit(lost_results(missing))
    park()

# Session close: the day is read out of the two tables it was written into and
# leaves as one batch. The script keeps no state between hops, so the turns are
# parked as their own leg and meet the round rows again in the same reply.
if phase == "close-turns" and op == "select" and not err:
    # The RAW role travels, empty included (GH #282). `or "user"` here was an
    # invention UPSTREAM of `SAID`: a row without a role arrived at
    # `drainable_turns` already labelled `user`, passed the filter and was
    # drained as something the user said -- while `turn_batch`, which filters
    # the raw rows, dropped the same row. Two lanes, two answers, over a row
    # nobody wrote. Carrying the role as it is lets the one filter decide, in
    # the one place that decides.
    turns = [{"role": str(r.get("role") or ""),
              "text": str(r.get("content") or ""),
              "interim": int(r.get("interim") or 0)} for r in rows_of(d)]
    # Backdated to the close arrival: the parked copy holds the session up to
    # the close, so the next prune takes it along with the day it copies.
    emit([cstore_bundle(
        [("c-close-w",
          {"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
           "row": {"turn_id": CLOSE_ID, "session_id": session, "iter": 0,
                   "role": "leg-close", "turn": json.dumps(turns), "fired": 0,
                   "recorded_at": boundary_of(turn_id)}}),
         ("c-close-read",
          {"operation": "select", "table": "round",
           "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired", "recorded_at"],
           "where": {"session_id": session}})],
        "close-fire", turn_id)])

if phase == "close-fire" and op == "bundle":
    # The batch and its evidence leave in ONE multi-send: the ledger row says
    # THIS session's day left as a batch at THIS boundary, and it is the one
    # thing the prune lane will ever trust (GH #76).
    emit([close_batch(bundle_rows_of(d, "c-close-read")),
          store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "batched",
                    "row": {"session_id": session,
                            "batched_at": boundary_of(turn_id)}},
                   "close-ledger", CLOSE_ID)])

# Prune (GH #76): one chain of two deletes per batched-and-aged session, all
# sessions in parallel. The chain state (boundary, then the turn count) rides
# in the hop id -- the script keeps no state between hops -- and the report is
# the rows_affected of the deletes themselves, never a re-read of what fell.
if phase == "prune-ledger" and op == "select" and not err:
    newest = {}
    for r in rows_of(d):
        s = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        b = str(r.get("batched_at") or "")
        if s and b and b > newest.get(s, ""):
            newest[s] = b
    if not newest:
        # No evidence, no cut -- and an answer anyway: the operator lane asked.
        emit([{"header": head("prune", "", extra={"session_id": "",
                                                  "pruned_turns": "0",
                                                  "pruned_rounds": "0",
                                                  "prune_boundary": ""}),
               "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                             "text": "pruned nothing: no batched session behind the age gate"}]}])
    # GH #419: the two deletes of one session are ONE message. Neither reads the
    # other -- the boundary they cut at is the same, and it comes from the ledger
    # -- so the chain of two hops only ever bought two replies to add up. The
    # report reads the two `rows_affected` out of `results[]` instead of out of
    # two hop headers.
    emit([cstore_bundle(
        [("c-prune-turns",
          {"operation": "delete", "table": "turns",
           "where": {"session_id": s, "recorded_at": {"lte": b}}}),
         ("c-prune-rounds",
          {"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
           "where": {"session_id": s, "recorded_at": {"lte": b}}})],
        "prune-cut", "prune|" + b, extra={"session_id": s})
          for s, b in newest.items()])

if phase == "prune-cut" and op == "bundle":
    parts = turn_id.split("|")
    if len(parts) != 2 or not parts[1]:
        park()
    legs = results_by_id(d)
    cut_turns = 0
    cut_rounds = 0
    for r in d.get("results") or []:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        n = int(r.get("rows_affected", 0) or 0)
        if str(r.get("tool_call_id") or "") == "c-prune-turns":
            cut_turns = n
        elif str(r.get("tool_call_id") or "") == "c-prune-rounds":
            cut_rounds = n
    if legs.get("c-prune-turns", {}).get("error_code") or \
            legs.get("c-prune-rounds", {}).get("error_code"):
        # A refused half is a half-pruned session, and the ledger must not say
        # otherwise: the mark is what stops the next round asking again.
        park()
    emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "batched",
                    "set": {"pruned_at": now},
                    "where": {"session_id": session,
                              "batched_at": {"lte": parts[1]}}},
                   "prune-mark", turn_id),
          {"header": head("prune", "", extra={"pruned_turns": str(cut_turns),
                                              "pruned_rounds": str(cut_rounds),
                                              "prune_boundary": parts[1]}),
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "pruned session %s: %s turns, %s rounds up to %s"
                                 % (session, cut_turns, cut_rounds, parts[1])}]}])

park()

window_turns.description: Rolling window: how many of the newest turns of the session enter the context. The cut runs in the store as order by id desc + limit.

window_bytes.description: Rolling window: byte cap over the turn texts. Counted from the newest turn backwards; whole turns are dropped, never truncated, and the newest turn is kept even when it alone exceeds the cap.

turn_chars.description: Per-turn character cap applied before the byte cap. A single pathological turn cannot eat the whole window.

tool_chars.description: Per-item character cap on tool RESULT texts before they enter the seam. A single large tool result would otherwise flood the context window past every window knob; the full text stays readable in the round table.

round_bytes.description: Byte cap over the whole tool round. Counted from the newest iteration backwards; what does not fit falls as a WHOLE iteration, because a tool_result whose tool_call was dropped is a malformed turn for every provider.

memory_chars.description: Character cap on the memory bundle where the bundle travels: the synthetic `memory_recall` tool result the ambient recall leg leaves as (GH #278). ONE cap over the whole result text, so under memory_form 'both' it bounds the readable block and the machine-readable form together rather than each of them separately. hop.memory_capped is measured on that result. The full bundle stays addressable in the round table.

max_iter.description: How many times a turn may re-enter the brain with a tool round. At the cap the seam leaves through the answer lane with hop.round_capped=1 instead of asking again - the seam opened the round, so the seam closes it.

round_idle_ms.description: Idle window of one tool round in milliseconds (default two minutes). A round whose last progress - the newest recorded_at of its rows - lies behind this window while its fan-in is still incomplete is closed at the NEXT message that reaches the cell anyway (the next result, the next turn, an in_round_sweep request): the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, then the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. Pure arithmetic, no timer of the template's own.

memory_tier.description: Memory leg. Empty = no memory leg: the recall port is not wired and the assembly waits for the window leg alone. '0' / '1' / '2' request that recall tier once per turn. What comes back reaches the brain as the result of a synthetic `memory_recall` call at the end of the round, never as durable system state (GH #278); system.memory carries the revocation of that slot and nothing else.

memory_call_tier.description: Recall tier of the memory TOOL (GH #78). The brain asks for memory itself with a `memory_recall` tool_call; the dispatcher routes it by name, and the cell behind that edge is the collector, which serves the call on the same recall port the per-turn leg uses and answers it with a tool_result under the original tool_call_id. The tier is configuration, never a model argument. Empty switches the tool off: every call is then answered with a typed error result instead of being asked into a void.

memory_form.description: Which form of the bundle reaches the brain in the synthetic `memory_recall` tool result: 'readable' the rendered block a model reads, 'json' the machine-readable bundle, 'both' the two joined by a newline. The collector renders nothing of its own; both forms come from the memory hive verbatim.

prune_after_ms.description: Age gate on the prune lane in milliseconds (default seven days). A session is pruned only when its close batch left the collector (the 'batched' ledger row is the evidence) AND that delivery is older than this gate. Without a ledger row nothing is ever pruned.

turn_write.description: Per-turn episodes, and since GH #298 (ruling Q11) the ONLY path from a conversation into an episodes table. On by default; '' or '0' switch it off, and off means nothing said in this session reaches a memory at all. Every stored turn - the inbound one and the answer - hands out ONE message per unwritten turn on route 'turn_write', in the shape a memory hive's writer port reads: one user/assistant turn, hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it. Model-free. Idempotence is the 'episode_written' column of the collector's own 'turns' table, guarded in the same emission as the episode it covers, so a re-delivered scan writes nothing twice. Wire the route to a memory hive's episode lane; leave it off only when no such consumer exists, or every turn emits a route nobody routes.

inline_extraction.description: The inline extraction contract (GH #525). Non-empty writes the shipped contract block to system.instructions.extraction on every turn assembly, which is what asks the brain for the ```memory block the memory hive's in_remember lane reads; empty writes nothing. Ships OFF because what cuts the block back out of the answer is a splitter between brain and dispatcher and this cell cannot see whether one stands behind it: talky switches it on, cogny has no splitter and leaves it off. The write carries no $replace marker, so the charter in instructions.reply is not touched. The block itself is byte-identical to the fence of templates/memory-hive/inline-contract.md.

context_window.description: The curator's budget: the context window of the configured model, in TOKENS. 0 or empty = curation OFF and the cell behaves exactly as it did before wave 11 - the per-item caps stay the only bound. Set it, and every assembly is projected against the budget and elides what does not fit, deterministically and without a model call.

curate_soft.description: The working mark, as a fraction of context_window. At or above it the curator elides in stages until the projection fits under it again. Conservative on purpose: retrieval degradation is measured long before a window is actually full.

curate_hard.description: The emergency mark, as a fraction of context_window. It changes no behaviour of its own - it is REPORTED as hop.curate_mark='hard' and means: the curator has run out of stages and the next thing that could give is prose. That is the signal a fold lane subscribes to.

keep_rounds.description: How many of the NEWEST tool iterations stay verbatim whatever the budget says. A curator that elides what the model is holding in its hands right now does not save context, it causes a retry.

recoverability.description: What may be elided, DECLARED per tool name and never guessed. Form: 'read_file:repeatable,write_file:env'. env = the effect is already in the environment and the result text is a receipt; repeatable = a read or a search that running again reproduces; unique = not reproducible, and the DEFAULT for every tool not named here. An undeclared tool therefore costs context, never correctness.

thread_recall.description: The thread tool: the model asks for an elided payload back by call id, round or substring, and the collector serves the call itself out of its own round table - the same bauform as the memory tool. Empty switches it off, and a call is then answered with a typed error instead of being asked into a void. A stub without a way back is worse than no stub at all, so switching this off should mean switching curation off.

thread_recall_budget.description: The share of context_window one turn's recalls may spend. Over it the call is REFUSED with a typed error naming the number - never truncated, because a silently halved recall is a lie about what the model was shown. Without a context_window the round byte cap stands in as the wall.

tool_menu.description: The tool menu this collector owns, as the provider-native JSON array the model is handed -- the same objects `system.tools.<name>.text` holds, in one string. Empty (the shipped default) means the menu lives in the brain and this cell writes no `system.tools` at all. Set it, and the collector becomes the owner of the slot: it emits the subtree with `$replace` on every assembly and the curator's stage 4 may stub the declarations of tools that went unused for `keep_rounds` iterations. That is the point of moving it -- tool declarations are the largest block in a real prompt (measured: 5267 characters against 3998 for everything else) and a curator that cannot reach them is a budget manager without a budget. A malformed value reads as EMPTY, never as half a menu.

tool_desc_chars.description: How much of a stubbed tool's description survives beside its name, in characters. A stub the model cannot read is a tool it will not call; one line is what says the tool exists and that its schema is one `thread_recall(call_id="tool:<name>")` away. Only stage 4 reads it.

tools.description: The tool names this agent DECLARES it uses (GH #464). At every tick of the menu lane the collector asks the tools hive for exactly these names and turns the answer into `system.tools` -- one durable write into the brain, not a per-turn cost. `["*"]` asks for everything the hive has. A comma string is read the same way as an array. Empty (the shipped default) asks for nothing at all, and so does a collector that carries a typed `tool_menu`: that knob is the manual override, and two writers on the same slot path would overwrite each other every round. A name the hive does not have comes back in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line in `log.jsonl` -- never as a silence.

curate_slot_chars.description: Size above which a `system.*` slot of this cell's OWN making becomes a stage-5 candidate, in characters. The protected families -- handover, persona, identity, instructions, plus `tools` (own stage) and `budget` (own sentence) -- are never candidates at any size or budget, which is what makes 'put the hard constraints in system' a promise rather than a hope. A candidate is CUT to its head and says so; it is never replaced by a reference, because a leaf sent from here overwrites the durable one in the brain and a curator may not revoke somebody else's state to shorten one prompt. 0 switches the stage off.

curate_budget_line.description: Tell the generator its budget instead of only enforcing it: one short deterministic sentence in `system.budget` naming tokens used, the window and what is left. No model, nothing to drift. "" or "0" sends the leaf EMPTY rather than not sending it -- `system.*` is durable and a number left standing from the last busy turn is worse than none. With `context_window` at 0 no leaf travels at all.

messages.description: The turns of what leaves. OPTIONAL since 1.4.0 (GH #458): the `pack` route carries `system.*` and nothing else, so the receiving `llm` cell upserts the slots and returns without an inference. Every other route still writes turns.

tools.description: The names this agent declares it uses, on the `schemas` route and nowhere else (GH #464). It is the whole body of the request: the tools hive keeps no table of who asks, so the caller says what it wants every time.

degraded.description: GH #343: "1" on a report the collector emits because it could NOT do what the lane asked -- today only when the store refused a read or a write. A parent that wants to render a failure differently from an answer branches on this key instead of parsing the text.

store_error.description: GH #343: the store's own `error_code` on a reply this lane refused to read as rows (`invalid_input`, `query_timeout`, `write_denied`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_column`, `constraint_violation`, `sql_error`, ...). Present exactly when `degraded` is.

store_operation.description: GH #343: the op the store refused, as `hop.operation` named it -- `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked.

curate_tools.description: How many tool DECLARATIONS stage 4 stubbed in this assembly (GH #451).

curate_slots.description: How many `system.*` slots stage 5 cut in this assembly (GH #451).

pack_owner.description: Who pushed the pack, taken from `envelope.reply_to` and never from the body. Rides on `pack` and on `pack_ack` alike (GH #458).

pack_slots.description: The slot names of one pack, sorted and comma-joined -- what was asked for, whether or not it was accepted (GH #458).

pack_unknown.description: The slot names a pack was refused for, sorted and comma-joined. Empty on an accepted pack, and present rather than absent so a CEL guard never fails on a missing key (GH #458).

error_code.description: Empty on an accepted pack, `slot_unknown` when a pack named a slot outside the writable list, `pack_empty` when it named none at all. `pack_ack` carries it always (GH #458).

asked_count.description: How many names one `schemas` request carried (GH #464).

menu_count.description: How many declarations the `menu` route wrote into `system.tools` (GH #464).

menu_self.description: The declarations on that menu that came from THIS cell rather than from the tools hive, comma-joined (GH #512): the tools the collector answers itself, `memory_recall` out of its own recall port and `thread_recall` out of its own slate. Empty rather than absent, for the same reason as `menu_unknown` one key down.

menu_answerers.description: WHO the menu was merged from, comma-joined and sorted (GH #529): one name per answerer this cell holds a submenu for. The menu is a union over answerers since 3.4.0 -- a tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is topology of the level that draws the edge, so the side that ANSWERS it is the side that declares it -- and this key is the receipt that says which of them the write actually stands on. Empty rather than absent, for the same reason as `menu_unknown` two keys down.

menu_unknown.description: The declared names NO answerer has anything under, comma-joined (GH #464, recomputed against the merged menu since GH #529). Before 3.4.0 this was per ANSWER, which made every tick of a two-answerer tree report the half of the list it had not asked that answerer for; a name is a finding only when nobody delivered it. Empty rather than absent, so an edge's CEL guard never fails on a missing hop key.

messages.description: The turns of whatever arrived. OPTIONAL since 1.4.0 (GH #458) and it has to be: the `in_pack` lane carries a durable `system.*` slot and NO turn beside it -- that is the shape an `llm` cell upserts without calling, and the shape `affinity`'s push lane emits. Requiring the key would refuse the pack at the delivery boundary, before this cell ever saw it. Every other lane still sends one; a body without turns simply carries no text, which the script already reads as the empty string.

system.description: The pack of durable slots on the `in_pack` lane, and the memory bundle's own subtree on `in_bundle`. Consumed on those two lanes and dropped on every other (GH #458, GH #252).

slot.description: The single-slot form of a pack (`in_pack`, GH #458): one slot name, merged over whatever `system` carried. It is a convenience and NOT a body of its own -- a UBF body has to carry `messages` or `system` (the substrate's anyOf, `meclaw-core::validate_ubf_body`), so a hand-written single slot rides beside an empty `"system": {}` and is dead-lettered as `invalid_ubf_body` without it.

content.description: The value of the single slot named by `slot` (`in_pack`, GH #458).

schemas.description: The declarations the tools hive answered with, on the `in_menu` lane: one `{name, description, parameters}` per name it has (GH #464). Provider-neutral -- this cell wraps them.

unknown.description: The declared names the tools hive has nothing under, verbatim (GH #464). Reported, never dropped.

tool_answerer.description: WHO answered a `in_schemas` question (GH #529) -- the mirror of the `context.tool_caller` the request carries. It keys the submenu row this cell stores, so several answerers' declarations are merged instead of replacing each other. Absent is the one-answerer shape every tree had before 3.4.0 and counts as the default answerer, so nothing wired earlier changes behaviour.

description.purpose: The context orchestrator of one agent: it decides what enters the LLM's context window and what leaves it. Rolling short-term turns of the session (user AND assistant, so a conversation can reference its own previous turns without retrieval), the memory bundle, the tool round, and a deterministic eviction policy over all three of them. Everything the brain sees leaves through ONE message on route 'brain' - and when the round has spent its iteration budget, that same seam leaves on 'answer' instead, so a runaway loop ends where it began. A round that lost a result does not park forever: when its last progress lies behind params.round_idle_ms, the next message that reaches the cell closes it - the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, and the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. A user turn arriving while a round of its session is open is written into the window but starts NO second assembly: it rides with the next regular assembly (hop.round_deferred=1 on that arrival) - at most one open brain call per session. On a close request the collector reads its own store back and hands the whole session on as one batch on route 'write', and writes the delivery into the 'batched' ledger in the same multi-send. On a prune request it cuts the rows of sessions that ledger names as delivered-and-aged, and reports the cut on route 'prune'. A tool the dispatcher classified as ASYNC (hop.async_calls) opens no fan-in expectation at all: it is acknowledged on the spot under its own tool_call_id, and a bundle that asked for nothing else is filed as already fired when the turn is going to be answered anyway - either because the model spoke beside the bundle (the dispatcher already sent that sentence as the interim answer) or because a HANDOFF call took the turn with it (hop.handoff_calls: an advisor's event, an escalation opening a fresh turn). Neither, and the round stays OPEN (GH #372): the acknowledgement completes the fan-in, the regular guard fires and the seam re-enters the brain for the iteration the model has not spent, because a round that ends without a word ends in silence - a bare fire-and-forget call like `remember` used to leave the channel with no answer at all. Its result comes back later on the in_advice lane as an EVENT with a consult_id, is assembled like a turn and opens a FRESH round, so the follow-up reaches the channel in the agent's own voice; the ids of the advice turns still in the window travel to the brain as system.consult.open, which is how a reply finds its way back to the right open question. Since 1.1.0 the assembly is also CURATED: before it leaves, the finished projection is measured against params.context_window and, over the soft mark, tool payloads whose recoverability is DECLARED are replaced in stages by stubs carrying a content hash and a thread_recall key - LLM-free, at every round rather than at a threshold, and never touching the conversation, system.*, a tool_call NAME or the newest params.keep_rounds iterations. Because no text is ever rewritten, the same question has the same answer basis before and after any number of curations.
description.use_when: Between an agent's inbound surface and its LLM, in place of a persona cell that only injects a system prompt and a prep cell that only mints a turn id. Wire the eleven entry lanes and the six exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates the hive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly, and the brain edge is ONE seam so an agent split can happen behind it later without re-cutting the collector). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool is a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in. No judgement about memory: the collector READS the recall bundle and it hands the closed session on unfiltered, but what is extracted and what is kept belongs to the receiver of the write batch. Eviction is deterministic policy, never a model judgement, and no CAP deletes: every cap is a read-time cut, the full value stays addressable in the round store. Rows fall only on the in_prune lane, only with delivery evidence in the batched ledger and behind the age gate - and the collector never fires that lane itself: no schedule, no self-initiated housekeeping, the parent tree decides whether a timer is wired to it. No timer and no schedule of the template's own anywhere: the in_round_sweep lane is an OCCASION a parent tree may provide, and a sweep that finds nothing stale emits nothing. No classification of the async class: the dispatcher declares it and this cell obeys the marker. No rendering of an advisor event: what arrives on in_advice enters the window as its text, and the correlation ids leave as raw data. No curation of the conversation and no prose: the curator elides declared-recoverable tool payloads and nothing else, it asks no model, and it removes no row - a stub answers its tool_call exactly like the payload did. What is not declared is unique and is never touched, so an undeclared tool costs context and never correctness. No fold: turning a round into prose is a lane this cell does not have.
description.emits_meaning: route cstore: store ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the state, hop.turn_id correlates the turn; both are promoted to context by the edge). route recall: the memory requests of this hive - one ambient request per turn (hop.memory_call_id empty) and one per memory_recall tool call (hop.memory_call_id = the tool_call_id, hop.recall_window_from / recall_window_to = the time range the MODEL asked for, GH #78). Both travel the same edge, so every key is always present and empty rather than absent. route brain: THE assembled context window - messages[] the rolling window followed by the tool round and, with params.memory_tier set, the ambient recall bundle as a synthetic memory_recall tool_call/tool_result pair at the end of it (GH #278: evidence of THIS round, under a call id derived from the bundle itself); system carries the revocation of system.memory - the empty leaf on the fixed path recall plus the $replace marker, and no bundle data at all - and, when advice turns are still in the window, system.consult.open with their raw correlation ids; hop.iter the loop counter for the next call, hop.window_turns / window_dropped / window_capped and hop.round_dropped / round_capped / memory_capped what the caps did, hop.round_stale=1 when the round was closed by the idle exit (a synthetic result travels in place of each lost one; a late real result wins over its stand-in), hop.round_deferred=1 when a deferred mid-round turn rides in this window for the first time (the stamp is cleared in the same multi-send). route answer: the brain's final turn on its way out after it has been written into the window - OR, with hop.round_capped=1, the assembled context of a round that reached params.max_iter and will not ask again. route write: one batch per closed session, messages[] the whole conversation in order, the raw round rows in the top-level slot 'rounds', hop.turn_count / round_count their sizes. route prune: one report per pruned session - hop.session_id, hop.pruned_turns, hop.pruned_rounds, hop.prune_boundary - or a single zero report when no session was eligible; the deletes themselves never leave the hive. An incomplete fan-in and a lost guard race emit NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal by design).
description.consumes_meaning: Eleven entry lanes, each named by hop.route on the port edge: in_turn (an inbound user turn), in_advice (an advisor's result or its question back, correlated by context.consult_id - the same chain as in_turn, filed under role 'advice' and opening a fresh round), in_bundle (the memory hive's bundle - the ambient leg of the turn, or the result of a memory_recall call when context.memory_call_id is set), in_calls (the assistant tool_call turn from the dispatcher; hop.async_calls names the ids this fan-in must NOT wait for, hop.handoff_calls the subset of those whose call ends the turn - GH #372), in_tool (one tool result: every `tool_result` turn of its `messages[]`, filed under the call id each answers -- a result carries no `system` slot and no top-level body slot, GH #252), in_memory_call (a memory_recall tool_call the dispatcher routed by name - the collector serves it itself on its own recall port, GH #78), in_thread_call (a thread_recall tool_call the dispatcher routed by name - the way back to a payload the curator elided out of THIS turn, served here because the collector owns the slate the stub points at, GH #245), in_answer (the brain's final turn), in_close (a session keeper's close request, carrying the session_id), in_prune (a timer's or operator's housekeeping request - the collector never schedules one itself), in_round_sweep (a timer's or operator's stuck-round re-check, the other occasion for the idle exit - equally never scheduled by the collector). Lanes are read before phases, because a message arriving over a port edge carries whatever col_phase its chain left in context. Store replies are dispatched by (context.col_phase, hop.operation); hop.rows_affected on a guarded update decides who fires - exactly once per turn and exactly once per tool round - and on the prune deletes it IS the report.
examples: turn 3 of a session -> insert user turn -> select the 12 newest turns -> leg-window -> gate -> guarded fire -> brain sees turns 1..3, so 'what did I say first?' is answered from the window and not from retrieval
window of 40 turns, params.window_turns=5 -> the store returns 5, hop.window_capped=1; a byte cap that cannot afford the 5th drops it and everything older, hop.window_dropped counts them
2 parallel tool calls -> 1 assistant row + 2 tool rows -> the round is complete -> guarded update wins once -> brain sees window + assistant turn + both results with hop.iter incremented
a 100 KB tool result -> the round row keeps all of it, the seam sees params.tool_chars of it and says hop.round_capped=1; the reader that wants the rest asks the store
a model that keeps asking for tools -> at iter == params.max_iter the seam emits route 'answer' with hop.round_capped=1 and everything collected so far, instead of a ninth brain call

params.memory_tier=0 -> the turn also fires a recall request; the bundle arrives on in_bundle, becomes the leg-memory row and enters the context window as the LAST tool_result of the round, answering a synthetic memory_recall call under a call id derived from the bundle itself (GH #278); system.memory carries only the revocation of the slot the bundle used to occupy

the session keeper closes generation 's1' -> in_close -> select turns of s1 -> park them as leg-close -> select round of s1 -> ONE message on route 'write' with every turn of the day and every round row beside it, plus the batched ledger row in the same multi-send

a timer fires in_prune seven days later -> the ledger names s1 as delivered and aged -> turns and round rows of s1 up to its close boundary fall, the living session s2 is untouched -> one report on route 'prune' with pruned_turns/pruned_rounds; without the ledger row the same request deletes NOTHING and reports zero

a tool dies mid-flight: 2 calls, 1 result, then silence -> the round parks; the next turn, the next result or an in_round_sweep request after params.round_idle_ms closes it - the missing call gets a synthetic 'tool result lost' result under its own tool_call_id, and the round fires regularly with hop.round_stale=1

a user turn arrives while a round runs -> it is written into the window, stamped deferred, and starts NO second assembly (one open brain call per session, the telephone model); the next regular assembly carries it with hop.round_deferred=1 and clears the stamp in the same multi-send

the brain asks for memory itself: a tool_call 'memory_recall' with {query, window_from, window_to} -> the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name like any other tool -> in_memory_call -> route 'recall' with the window as recall_window_from/_to and the call id as memory_call_id -> the bundle returns on in_bundle and becomes the tool_result of that call -> the round completes and re-enters the brain through the same seam

the same call with params.memory_call_tier empty -> answered on the spot with a typed error result under its own tool_call_id, because a call that cannot be served is a failed call, not a hung round; with no recall edge wired at all the request is unroutable and the round ends in the idle exit of GH #103 instead

a bundle of one consult_cogny call with hop.async_calls='c1' AND a sentence beside it -> the assistant row is written as fired=1 and c1 is answered on the spot with 'handed to the async lane' -> no round is open, no sweep finds one, and the turn is over with the interim answer the dispatcher sent

the same bundle with NO text beside it and hop.handoff_calls empty (GH #372) -> the row stays OPEN, the acknowledgement completes the fan-in, the guard fires and the brain gets the iteration it has not spent -- bounded by params.max_iter, which leaves on route 'answer' with hop.round_capped=1 when it is spent

a bare escalate_to_deep call, no text, hop.handoff_calls='e1' -> filed as fired=1 like the first example: the answer comes from the turn the escalation opens, so this round is over without a word of its own
the same bundle plus a web_search c2 -> the assistant row stays open, c1 is acknowledged at once and the round completes as soon as c2 answers

the advisor answers hours later: in_advice with context.consult_id='k-7' -> an 'advice' turn is written into the window, the memory leg fires like on any turn, the gate closes and the seam hands the brain a FRESH round that verbalises the result in the channel

the advisor asks back instead: the same lane, the same id -> the window carries the question and the brain is shown system.consult.open=['k-7'], so its next consult call can pass that id and the advisor keeps one thread

twenty rounds of large file reads with params.context_window=200000 and params.recoverability='read_file:repeatable,write_file:env': at half the budget the env payloads of every round older than the newest two are replaced by '[elided tool_result w7 - 4006 chars - tool=write_file - kind=env - sha256:2f5d... - recall: thread_recall(call_id="w7")]', and the seam reports curate_mark=soft, curate_stage=1, curate_elided and curate_saved

the model needs an elided result back: it calls thread_recall(call_id) like any other tool, the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name, and this cell serves it out of its own round table - the ORIGINAL text, uncapped, under the original tool_call_id; over params.thread_recall_budget the call is refused with a typed error instead of being silently halved

the provider omits its usage field: the trigger falls back to a chars/4 estimate marked tokens_estimated=1 - a LOWER bound, so it can fire late but never early - and the turn leaves normally instead of parking on a threshold edge that could not evaluate
